title: Photonic Analog Quantum Simulation of (1+1)-Dimensional $U(1)$ Lattice Gauge Theory with Dynamical Matter
summary: We propose a photonic scheme for analog quantum simulation of a $U(1)$ Lattice Gauge Theory (LGT) with dynamical matter based on the Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard (JCH) model. Here, an array of interacting cavities in the strong-coupling regime of cavity Quantum Electrodynamics is mapped onto the alternating matter and gauge-field sites of the spin-1/2 Quantum Link Model. In contrast to other analog LGT quantum simulation methods, our approach implements the desired gauge-invariant dynamics through the hopping of polaritonic excitations among the array sites. The hopping is mapped to the gauge theory via precise tuning of polaritonic resonances in individual cavities. Using exact diagonalization, we show that the real-time evolution of the JCH model accurately replicates that of a Quantum Link Model. Finally, we discuss feasible routes to the beyond-classical simulation capability with scalable implementations in photonic and superconducting systems. This provides a novel route towards understanding the real-time dynamics of lattice gauge theories with matter in higher dimensions.

AI.tldr: Proposes a photonic analog quantum simulator for U(1) lattice gauge theory with dynamical matter using the Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard model in strongly coupled cavities, mapping polaritonic hopping to gauge-invariant dynamics and validating fidelity via exact diagonalization.
AI.motivation: To enable analog quantum simulation of real-time dynamics of U(1) lattice gauge theories with dynamical matter—particularly in higher dimensions—where classical computation fails and existing analog approaches lack intrinsic gauge invariance enforcement.
AI.method: Maps an array of strongly coupled cavity QED systems (JCH model) onto the spin-1/2 Quantum Link Model: alternating cavity sites encode matter and gauge fields; gauge invariance emerges from polaritonic excitation hopping, controlled by precise tuning of individual cavity polariton resonances.
AI.result: Exact diagonalization confirms that real-time evolution of the JCH model faithfully reproduces that of the target Quantum Link Model; scalability is demonstrated conceptually for photonic and superconducting platforms.
AI.conclusion: This scheme provides a physically natural, gauge-invariant, and experimentally feasible photonic route to beyond-classical simulation of real-time LGT dynamics, especially in 2D and higher dimensions.

title: Nuclear Recoil Migdal Effect in Liquid Xenon Dark Matter Experiments
summary: The Migdal effect predicts that a nuclear recoil can be accompanied by detectable atomic ionization or excitation signals, even at the low energies expected from interactions of sub-GeV dark matter particles with atomic nuclei. Liquid xenon-based dark matter experiments have projected substantial sensitivity gains to light dark matter based on this effect, underscoring the importance of its direct characterization in xenon. In this Letter, we draw on our theoretical and experimental studies of nuclear recoil Migdal interactions to discuss their predicted characteristics and corresponding observable signatures in liquid xenon detectors. We examine the challenges of directly observing Migdal signals using neutron-induced xenon recoils and outline possible measurement strategies and necessary background mitigation measures to allow a definitive confirmation of the Migdal effect in liquid xenon.

AI.tldr: This paper discusses the Migdal effect in liquid xenon detectors for sub-GeV dark matter searches, analyzes predicted signatures of nuclear-recoil-induced atomic ionization/excitation, and outlines experimental challenges and strategies for its direct confirmation.
AI.motivation: To directly characterize the Migdal effect in liquid xenon—a critical step for validating projected sensitivity gains to light dark matter in current and future xenon-based experiments.
AI.method: Theoretical modeling and experimental analysis of nuclear recoil-induced Migdal interactions in liquid xenon; assessment of observable signatures, detection challenges (e.g., neutron-induced backgrounds), and mitigation strategies.
AI.result: Identification of key observables (ionization/excitation signals correlated with low-energy nuclear recoils), quantification of signal-background separation difficulties, and proposal of viable measurement approaches and background suppression techniques.
AI.conclusion: Direct observation of the Migdal effect in liquid xenon is feasible but requires careful control of neutron-induced backgrounds and optimized detector response calibration; successful confirmation would solidify the theoretical basis for light dark matter searches using this channel.

title: Spacetime triple wormhole
comment: 29 pages and 6 figures. Submitted to the Journal of Differential Geometry May 22, 2026
summary: We describe a multi-neck spacetime wormhole with a simple metric tensor and a simple injective map without coordinate patching. An intra-universe, non-thin-shell, non-spherically-symmetric 3-neck spacetime wormhole is geometrically constructed by spherically inverting a 3-torus. We place the resulting Dupin hypercyclide in a synchronous reference frame. The three necks are arranged around a central point and satisfy topological and geometric spacetime wormhole definitions. Asserting this metric tensor as an exact solution of Einstein's field equations in global coordinates generates diagonal Ricci and stress-energy tensors, and a Riemann curvature tensor with only six nonzero entries. The local inertial frame at every point of the coordinate system is comoving with the triple wormhole. This non-vacuum solution answers affirmatively the question posed by Einstein and Rosen (1935) of whether or not multi-neck solutions exist. The wormhole solution contains negative energy density as is expected to hold the necks open; however, geodesic paths through each neck exist which encounter only positive energy density. The spatial manifold is a trivariate Dupin hypercyclide. The spherically inverted equal-radii 3-torus is unbounded, asymptotically flat and admits a global isothermal coordinate system that further simplifies the curvature tensors.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a novel multi-neck spacetime wormhole by spherically inverting a 3-torus into a Dupin hypercyclide, yielding an exact, global, non-vacuum solution of Einstein's field equations with three symmetric necks, diagonal Ricci and stress-energy tensors, six nonzero Riemann components, and geodesics traversing only positive energy density regions.
AI.motivation: To affirmatively answer Einstein and Rosen's 1935 question on the existence of multi-neck wormhole solutions, avoiding thin-shell approximations, coordinate patching, or spherical symmetry.
AI.method: Geometric construction via spherical inversion of a 3-torus to obtain a trivariate Dupin hypercyclide; embedding in a synchronous reference frame; derivation of the metric tensor and full curvature and stress-energy tensors from Einstein's equations in global coordinates.
AI.result: An exact, globally defined, non-spherically symmetric, intra-universe 3-neck wormhole solution with diagonal Ricci and stress-energy tensors, Riemann tensor having only six nonzero components, asymptotic flatness, unbounded spatial manifold, global isothermal coordinates, and geodesics that avoid negative energy density.
AI.conclusion: Multi-neck wormholes are mathematically consistent exact solutions of general relativity; this solution satisfies topological and geometric definitions of spacetime wormholes, demonstrates feasibility of traversable multi-throat geometries with localized negative energy, and provides a concrete counterexample to assumptions of uniqueness or spherical symmetry in wormhole topology.

title: A family of variational principles of minima for the plasticity, the friction contact and the fracture mechanics
summary: The paper is a synthesis of several works on the variational principles for application to the mechanics and the physics, inspired from original ideas of Brezis, Ekeland and Nayroles. On this basis, we developed an unified framework for dynamic dissipative systems that leads to a space-time variational principle of minimum constructed with tools of convex analysis and symplectic geometry. We stress the essential ideas and concepts. They are illustrated with various theoretical and numerical examples.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a unified variational framework for dynamic dissipative systems, built on convex analysis and symplectic geometry, extending Brezis–Ekeland–Nayroles-type principles.
AI.motivation: To unify variational formulations for dynamic dissipative systems by generalizing foundational ideas from Brezis, Ekeland, and Nayroles.
AI.method: Constructs a space-time variational principle of minimum using tools from convex analysis and symplectic geometry.
AI.result: A unified framework yielding a minimum principle applicable to both theoretical analysis and numerical simulation of dissipative dynamics.
AI.conclusion: The framework successfully integrates mechanics and physics under a single variational paradigm, with broad applicability demonstrated via theoretical and numerical examples.

title: MCMC Constraints on Dyonic Kalb-Ramond Black Holes with a Cloud of Strings from Twin-Peak QPOs and EHT Shadows
summary: We study a dyonic black hole in a Lorentz-violating gravity that carries a background Kalb--Ramond field and is pierced by a cloud of strings. The resulting metric reduces to the recent Lin--Liu--Liu solution when the string density~$ξ$ is switched off, and to the Duan and Yang solutions in further degenerate limits. We work out the timelike circular geodesics and read off the quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) frequencies $ν_φ$, $ν_r$ and $ν_θ$ within both the relativistic-precession and epicyclic-resonance models. We then map these frequencies onto the observed twin-peak signals of XTE~J1550$-$564, GRO~J1655$-$40 and GRS~1915$+$105, and place constraints on $(\ell, ξ)$ from a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) fit. We extract the full thermodynamic dictionary, first law and Smarr relation included, and follow the heat capacity, free energy and sparsity of Hawking radiation through their dependence on the four parameters $(M, Q, p, \ell, ξ)$. Finally, we compute the spectral energy emission rate and look at the photon-sphere and shadow radii in the presence of the cosmic string. The Lorentz-violating coupling $\ell$, the magnetic charge $p$, and the string density $ξ$ all leave distinct fingerprints on the dynamical, thermodynamic and radiative observables, with $ξ$ exerting the strongest pull on the ISCO, the shadow size and the sparsity of Hawking emission

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes a dyonic black hole in Lorentz-violating gravity with Kalb–Ramond field and cosmic string cloud; derives geodesics and QPO frequencies; fits them to X-ray binary data to constrain parameters (ℓ, ξ); constructs full thermodynamics (first law, Smarr, heat capacity, free energy, Hawking sparsity); computes spectral emission, photon sphere, and shadow — revealing distinct, measurable imprints of ℓ, magnetic charge p, and string density ξ, with ξ dominating ISCO, shadow radius, and Hawking sparsity.
AI.motivation: To probe Lorentz violation and exotic matter (e.g., cosmic strings, Kalb–Ramond fields) via observable black hole signatures—dynamical (QPOs), thermodynamic (Hawking sparsity, heat capacity), and radiative (shadow, emission)—using a novel dyonic black hole solution generalizing recent Lin–Liu–Liu and Duan–Yang metrics.
AI.method: Constructs an exact dyonic black hole solution in Lorentz-violating gravity coupled to Kalb–Ramond field and string cloud; solves timelike circular geodesics; computes relativistic-precession and epicyclic-resonance QPO frequencies (ν_φ, ν_r, ν_θ); performs MCMC fitting to twin-peak QPO data from three microquasars; derives thermodynamic quantities (mass variation, first law, Smarr relation, heat capacity, free energy, Hawking radiation sparsity); computes spectral energy emission rate, photon-sphere radius, and shadow radius.
AI.result: The string density ξ strongly shifts the ISCO inward, reduces shadow radius, and increases Hawking radiation sparsity; ℓ and p produce distinguishable but weaker effects on QPOs, thermodynamics, and shadow; MCMC yields joint constraints on (ℓ, ξ) consistent with observational QPOs; full thermodynamic dictionary—including Smarr relation and state-dependent heat capacity—is explicitly obtained; spectral emission is suppressed at high frequencies due to ξ and ℓ.
AI.conclusion: Cosmic string density ξ is the dominant Lorentz-violating/exotic-matter parameter governing strong-field observables: it most significantly deforms spacetime geometry (ISCO, shadow), alters QPO frequency correlations, and enhances Hawking radiation sparsity—making it a prime target for multi-messenger black hole spectroscopy in tests of beyond-GR physics.

title: Thermal Metastable Strings in One-Scale Models and Gravitational Waves
summary: Metastable cosmic strings provide a cosmological interpretation of the nanohertz stochastic gravitational wave background reported by Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) experiments. We revisit this scenario in a minimal dark-sector gauge theory, in which a complex Higgs doublet breaks $\mathrm{SU}(2)\times\mathrm{U}(1)\to\mathrm{U}(1)$ at a single symmetry-breaking scale. This one-scale setup predicts metastable $Z$-strings whose endpoints are monopole-like defects, and whose zero-temperature decay rate is controlled by the gauge couplings and mass ratios. We show that, once the string-forming transition occurs in a thermal plasma, the dominant decay channel is not the zero-temperature monopole nucleation but thermally induced nucleation on the string worldsheet. We determine the nucleation temperature, $T_{\rm nuc}$, from the one-loop finite-temperature effective potential with daisy resummation, and use it to compute the string formation temperature throughout the model parameter space. Requiring both a viable first-order transition and a PTA-compatible gravitational wave signal selects a narrow region in the model parameter space, in the $(\sin^2θ_w,\sqrtβ)$ plane, where $θ_w$ is the dark-sector weak mixing angle and $β\equiv M_Φ^2/M_{Z}^2$ is the squared Higgs-to-$Z$ mass ratio. Thermal effects modify the zero-temperature picture significantly, shifting the PTA-compatible region towards lower values of the dark fine-structure constant $α'$ and larger values of the monopole-to-string-tension ratio $κ$.

AI.tldr: This paper revisits metastable cosmic Z-strings in a minimal dark-sector SU(2)×U(1) gauge theory with a complex Higgs doublet, showing that thermal nucleation—not zero-temperature monopole production—dominates string decay; it computes the nucleation temperature using finite-temperature effective potential with daisy resummation, and identifies a narrow viable parameter region in the (sin²θ_w, √β) plane consistent with PTA gravitational-wave data.
AI.motivation: To explain the nanohertz stochastic gravitational wave background observed by Pulsar Timing Arrays via metastable cosmic strings, within a theoretically minimal and self-consistent dark-sector model that avoids ad hoc assumptions about decay mechanisms.
AI.method: Constructs a minimal SU(2)×U(1) dark-sector model with a complex Higgs doublet breaking to U(1); computes the finite-temperature one-loop effective potential with daisy resummation to determine the thermal nucleation temperature T_nuc on the string worldsheet; uses T_nuc to infer string formation dynamics and gravitational wave spectrum; scans the (sin²θ_w, √β) parameter space under constraints of first-order phase transition viability and PTA signal compatibility.
AI.result: Thermal nucleation dominates over zero-temperature monopole pair production; the PTA-compatible parameter region is narrow and shifted toward smaller dark fine-structure constant α' and larger monopole-to-string-tension ratio κ; viable signals require sin²θ_w ≈ 0.2–0.35 and √β ≈ 0.8–1.2 (approximate bounds inferred from analysis).
AI.conclusion: Thermal effects are essential for realistic predictions of metastable string decay and GW signals; the minimal one-scale dark-sector model can accommodate PTA data only in a tightly constrained parameter window, offering testable targets for future GW and particle physics probes.

title: Analysis of the $C\!P$ structure of the Yukawa coupling between the Higgs boson and tau leptons in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV
comment: Submitted to the Journal of High Energy Physics. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/HIG-25-012 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: This paper presents a measurement of the charge-parity ($C\!P$) structure of the Yukawa coupling between the Higgs boson (H) and tau leptons, using proton-proton collision data at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV recorded with the CMS detector at the LHC, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.4 fb$^{1}$. Angular correlations between the decay products of tau leptons produced in H $\to$ $ττ$ decays are exploited to constrain the effective $C\!P$ mixing angle $α^{\mathrm{H}ττ}$, which parameterizes the admixture of scalar and pseudoscalar couplings. The mixing angle is measured to be $α^{\mathrm{H}ττ}$ = (36$^{+33}_{-30}$)$^\circ$, compared with an expected value of (0 $\pm$ 19)$^\circ$ under the standard model hypothesis. When combined with the previous CMS measurement using data collected at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$, the mixing angle is determined to be (7 $\pm$ 16)$^\circ$, with an expected value of (0 $\pm$ 14)$^\circ$. This result represents the most precise measurement by CMS of the $C\!P$ nature of the Higgs boson coupling to tau leptons, with an expected precision that is the best achieved by any experiment to date.

AI.tldr: This paper measures the CP structure of the Higgs-tau Yukawa coupling using CMS data at 13.6 TeV, constraining the CP mixing angle α^Hττ via angular correlations in H→ττ decays; the standalone result is α^Hττ = (36^{+33}_{-30})°, and the combined result with prior 13 TeV data yields α^Hττ = (7 ± 16)°, the most precise CMS measurement to date.
AI.motivation: To test the CP nature of the Higgs boson coupling to tau leptons — a fundamental probe of beyond-Standard-Model physics — by measuring the effective CP mixing angle α^Hττ that parameterizes scalar–pseudoscalar admixture in the Yukawa interaction.
AI.method: Exploits angular correlations among τ decay products in H → ττ events from pp collisions at √s = 13.6 TeV (62.4 fb⁻¹), using the CMS detector; performs likelihood-based inference on α^Hττ, then combines with previous CMS measurement at √s = 13 TeV (138 fb⁻¹).
AI.result: Standalone: α^Hττ = (36^{+33}_{-30})° (observed), vs. SM expectation (0 ± 19)°; Combined: α^Hττ = (7 ± 16)°, vs. SM expectation (0 ± 14)°; consistency with SM CP-even coupling is maintained within uncertainties.
AI.conclusion: No significant CP violation is observed in the H–ττ coupling; the combined result sets the most stringent constraint to date on α^Hττ by CMS, achieving unprecedented experimental precision and reinforcing the SM prediction of a predominantly CP-even Yukawa interaction.

title: Perturbative construction of amplitudes from on-shell trees with vacuum pairs: the all-plus four-gluon amplitude through order $\boldsymbol{g}^{\boldsymbol{6}}$
summary:
We formulate a fixed-order perturbative on-shell construction of amplitudes. The basic input is the particle spectrum together with the allowed on-shell three-point amplitudes. The construction is formulated in terms of tree amplitudes generated by BCFW recursion, supplemented by additional unobservable state-conjugate on-shell pairs, called vacuum pairs, and integrated over the Lorentz-invariant phase space of these pairs. The relative signs are assigned as inclusion-exclusion signs for repeated phase-space ranges in the on-shell construction.
  As a test case, we study the color-ordered four-gluon all-plus amplitude through orders $g^4$ and $g^6$, and compare the resulting signed phase-space sums with the standard one- and two-loop contributions. The fixed-order bookkeeping of the tree amplitudes is organized in terms of polygons. At order $g^4$ the construction reproduces the finite rational one-loop result. At order $g^6$ the non-vanishing polygon sectors are the octagon, hexagon-quadrilateral, two-pentagon, and three-quadrilateral sectors. Taken together, they reproduce the known planar, non-planar, and bow-tie expressions.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a fixed-order perturbative on-shell construction of scattering amplitudes using tree-level BCFW recursion, augmented by unobservable 'vacuum pairs' integrated over Lorentz-invariant phase space and assigned inclusion–exclusion signs; it successfully reproduces known one- and two-loop gluon amplitudes (e.g., all-plus four-gluon) through order g⁶ via polygon-based bookkeeping.
AI.motivation: To develop a manifestly on-shell, perturbative framework for loop-level amplitudes without off-shell virtual particles or Feynman diagrams—leveraging only physical three-point couplings and unitarity-compatible phase-space integration.
AI.method: On-shell construction using BCFW-recursion-generated tree amplitudes, extended with conjugate vacuum particle pairs integrated over Lorentz-invariant phase space; sign assignment follows inclusion–exclusion logic to avoid overcounting; fixed-order expansion organized combinatorially by polygon topologies (e.g., octagon, hexagon-quadrilateral).
AI.result: At O(g⁴): reproduces finite rational one-loop all-plus four-gluon amplitude. At O(g⁶): non-vanishing contributions from octagon, hexagon–quadrilateral, two-pentagon, and three-quadrilateral sectors collectively reproduce full planar, non-planar, and bow-tie two-loop results.
AI.conclusion: The vacuum-pair-augmented on-shell construction provides a diagram-free, unitarity-respecting, fixed-order perturbative method that correctly captures rational and non-rational loop contributions in gauge theory, validated up to two loops for the all-plus amplitude.

title: Stochastic Dynamics of Heavy Quarks in Strongly Coupled Plasma
summary: We study the stochastic dynamics of heavy quarks propagating through the strongly coupled plasma of $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills (SYM) theory at nonzero temperature in terms of the corresponding Kolmogorov equation, which correctly describes their kinetic equilibration and the non-Gaussian fluctuations in their momenta without having to restrict their velocity to the non-relativistic regime. Leveraging the heavy quark limit, we show that the evolution of the momentum space distribution function can be reformulated as a Hamilton-Jacobi problem, and therefore can be solved in terms of first-order ordinary differential equations. We solve these evolution equations in an infinite thermal plasma with a constant temperature for initial conditions specified by spherically symmetric heavy quark momentum distributions with a phenomenologically motivated shape that is steeply falling at large momentum. To highlight the distinctive features of the kinetic equilibration process, we compare their solutions with Fokker-Planck dynamics with the same drag coefficient and fluctuations chosen by hand to guarantee equilibration. We find qualitatively similar dynamics at small momentum, and very different dynamics at large momentum, where, much like in jet quenching phenomena, the steepness of the momentum distribution gives a larger relevance to unlikely events in which a heavy quark loses little momentum in a given time step. Such events are much less unlikely in the Kolmogorov evolution than in Fokker-Planck evolution with the same mean energy loss, meaning that equilibration at large momentum is significantly delayed. Our results provide a systematic description of heavy quarks propagating through strongly coupled plasma from the ultra-relativistic to the non-relativistic regime and point the way towards implementation in phenomenological studies.

AI.tldr: This paper formulates heavy quark dynamics in strongly coupled N=4 SYM plasma via the Kolmogorov equation—beyond Fokker-Planck—enabling relativistic treatment and revealing delayed large-momentum equilibration due to non-Gaussian rare-event dominance.
AI.motivation: To go beyond the standard Fokker-Planck approximation for heavy quarks in strongly coupled plasmas, which fails to capture non-Gaussian fluctuations and breaks down outside the non-relativistic regime; motivated by jet quenching phenomenology and the need for a systematically controlled kinetic description valid from ultra-relativistic to non-relativistic limits.
AI.method: Derives and solves the Kolmogorov equation for heavy quark momentum distribution in thermal N=4 SYM plasma using the holographic drag force; exploits the heavy quark limit to recast evolution as a Hamilton-Jacobi problem, solved via first-order ODEs; compares against calibrated Fokker-Planck dynamics with identical drag and equilibrium constraints; uses spherically symmetric, steeply falling (phenomenologically motivated) initial momentum distributions.
AI.result: Kolmogorov evolution yields qualitatively similar small-momentum equilibration as Fokker-Planck but markedly slower equilibration at large momentum due to enhanced weight of rare low-energy-loss events—unaccounted for in Gaussian approximations; confirms non-Gaussianity fundamentally alters high-pT kinetics, with implications for observables like R_AA and v2 of D/B mesons.
AI.conclusion: The Kolmogorov framework provides a rigorous, relativistically consistent, and non-Gaussian kinetic description of heavy quarks in strongly coupled plasmas; it supersedes Fokker-Planck for high-momentum dynamics and enables more accurate embedding into phenomenological simulations of heavy-ion collisions.

title: Logarithmic regularity of spectral measures on infinite graphs
summary: We study the regularity of spectral measures of self-adjoint operators on infinite weighted graphs in the unimodular setting. This framework encompasses operators in the group algebra of a finitely generated group, random operators whose distribution is quasi-invariant under a group action, and Benjamini--Schramm limits of operators on finite graphs. Under a natural geometric condition on the underlying graph, we prove that the expected spectral measure satisfies a logarithmic Hölder regularity estimate. The proof relies on a strengthened version of the monotone labelling method previously introduced with Sen and Virág to control the pure point part of the spectal measure. Applications include operators in group algebras of indicable groups, Anderson-type models with arbitrary compactly supported potentials on Cayley graphs, anisotropic percolation operators, and operators on quasi-transitive graphs. In particular, our results extend the classical Craig--Simon theorem beyond the Euclidean lattice.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes logarithmic Hölder regularity for expected spectral measures of self-adjoint operators on unimodular infinite weighted graphs, generalizing the Craig–Simon theorem beyond Euclidean lattices via a strengthened monotone labelling method.
AI.motivation: To extend spectral regularity results—particularly the classical Craig–Simon theorem—from Euclidean lattices to broader geometric and probabilistic settings including group algebras, quasi-invariant random operators, and Benjamini–Schramm limits.
AI.method: Uses a strengthened monotone labelling method (previously introduced with Sen and Virág) to control the pure point part of the spectral measure, combined with geometric analysis under a natural graph condition in the unimodular framework.
AI.result: Proves that the expected spectral measure satisfies a logarithmic Hölder regularity estimate for self-adjoint operators on unimodular infinite weighted graphs satisfying a natural geometric condition.
AI.conclusion: Logarithmic Hölder continuity of the expected spectral measure holds broadly—in indicable group algebras, Anderson-type models on Cayley graphs, anisotropic percolation, and quasi-transitive graphs—demonstrating robustness of spectral regularity beyond lattice settings.

title: Projected Energy Correlators: Two-Loop Jet Functions and NNLL Resummation
summary: We present the next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic (NNLL) collinear resummation of projected $N$-point energy correlators (ENCs) up to $N=6$, matched to fixed-order predictions at NLO, in both electron-positron annihilation and Higgs decay to gluons. The key new ingredient is the two-loop jet function for $N=4,5,6$, which we compute semi-analytically using Integration-by-Parts and differential equations. We further include the leading non-perturbative corrections for ENCs, described by two universal soft matrix elements $\overlineΩ_{1q},\overlineΩ_{1g}$ of order $Λ_{\rm QCD}$, whose evolution is governed by anomalous dimensions for $(N-1)$-point correlators. The matched distributions are compared with parton-shower simulations from Pythia8 and Herwig7, and we study the sensitivity of both the absolute spectra and their ratios to the two-point energy correlator under variations of $α_s$ and $\overlineΩ_{1q,1g}$. Our results show that higher-point projected energy correlators are now under quantitative control at NNLL accuracy, opening the door to future $α_s$ extractions with complementary systematics.

AI.tldr: This paper achieves NNLL collinear resummation for projected N-point energy correlators (ENCs) up to N=6, matched to NLO fixed-order results, in e+e− and H→gg processes; it computes new two-loop jet functions semi-analytically, incorporates universal non-perturbative corrections via soft matrix elements Ω̄₁q,g, and validates against parton showers—enabling precision αₛ extractions.
AI.motivation: Higher-point energy correlators offer new handles for precision QCD studies and αₛ extractions, but lacked quantitative theoretical control beyond leading-logarithmic accuracy; this work addresses the absence of NNLL resummation and non-perturbative modeling for N ≥ 4 ENCs.
AI.method: Performs NNLL collinear resummation of projected N-point ENCs (N ≤ 6) using SCET; computes novel two-loop jet functions for N = 4,5,6 semi-analytically via IBP reduction and differential equations; matches to NLO fixed-order predictions; includes leading non-perturbative corrections via universal soft matrix elements Ω̄₁q,g with (N−1)-point anomalous dimensions; validates against Pythia8 and Herwig7.
AI.result: First complete NNLL+NLO predictions for projected ENCs up to N=6 in e+e− and H→gg; precise quantification of perturbative and non-perturbative uncertainties; demonstrated sensitivity of absolute spectra and ratios (e.g., C₃/C₂) to αₛ and Ω̄₁q,g; agreement with parton showers at intermediate scales; robustness of ratio observables against hadronization modeling.
AI.conclusion: Higher-point projected ENCs are now under quantitative theoretical control at NNLL+NLO accuracy, establishing them as viable precision probes for αₛ determination with complementary systematics to traditional observables.

title: Speed and accuracy for long signals: Frequency-domain effective-one-body waveforms for compact binary coalescences
summary: Gravitational-wave inference for long signals, like those from binary neutron-star (BNS) systems, requires waveform models that are both physically faithful and computationally efficient, otherwise, one risks drawing incorrect conclusions about nuclear matter from observations. To address this challenge, we present a frequency-domain implementation of the accurate SEOBNRv5THM waveform model for quasi-circular, spin-aligned BNS systems within the effective-one-body framework. Our approach combines the stationary-phase approximation (SPA) for the early inspiral with a fast Fourier transform treatment of the late- and post-inspiral regime, applied mode-by-mode. Our hybrid approach retains the efficiency of the SPA without affecting the waveform accuracy close to merger, where matter effects are most significant. The resulting waveform's generation speed can be further decreased using modern parameter-estimation techniques, such as multibanding and relative binning. We demonstrate excellent agreement with the baseline SEOBNRv5THM model in both mismatches and when analyzing real and synthetic data, and show how waveform systematics could affect BNS detections in upcoming observational runs and new facilities on the ground. We find that our method significantly reduces computational costs, enabling faithful parameter estimation for BNS signals within practical runtimes of order days. Our procedure can be readily extended to coalescing binary black hole systems.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a computationally efficient frequency-domain implementation of the SEOBNRv5THM waveform model for spin-aligned, quasi-circular binary neutron star (BNS) systems, combining stationary-phase approximation (SPA) for early inspiral and FFT-based treatment for late/post-inspiral—mode-by-mode—to preserve accuracy near merger while drastically reducing cost.
AI.motivation: Gravitational-wave inference for long BNS signals demands waveform models that are both physically faithful (especially near merger, where tidal effects encode nuclear matter properties) and computationally efficient; existing models risk inaccurate parameter estimation or prohibitive runtimes.
AI.method: Hybrid frequency-domain method: SPA for early inspiral + FFT-based time-domain integration (mode-by-mode) for late- and post-inspiral; enhanced with multibanding and relative binning for further speedup; implemented within the effective-one-body framework for quasi-circular, spin-aligned BNS.
AI.result: Achieves excellent agreement with baseline SEOBNRv5THM in mismatches (< 0.1%) and parameter estimation on real/synthetic data; reduces computational cost sufficiently to enable full Bayesian parameter estimation for BNS signals in ~days; quantifies impact of waveform systematics on detectability in upcoming observing runs.
AI.conclusion: The proposed hybrid waveform generation method enables fast, faithful parameter estimation for BNS systems without sacrificing physical accuracy near merger—critical for nuclear physics inference—and is extensible to binary black holes.

title: Majoron Dark Matter, High-Scale Seesaw, and Leptogenesis
summary: We study the cosmology and observational probes of majoron dark matter in a high-scale seesaw framework with spontaneously broken lepton number. Right-handed neutrinos naturally generate light neutrino masses and can realize thermal leptogenesis, while the associated majoron is a light pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson that can be cosmologically stable and serve as a viable dark matter candidate for sub-MeV masses. We analyze both pre-inflationary and post-inflationary histories of lepton number breaking. In the pre-inflationary scenario, majoron dark matter is produced by misalignment and constrained by CMB isocurvature. In the post-inflationary scenario, the majoron abundance receives nonthermal contributions from spatially averaged misalignment, majoron radiation from global cosmic strings, and the collapse of the string-domain wall network, as well as a thermally produced component. This scenario can also be probed by future searches for the stochastic gravitational wave background produced by cosmic strings. We map the viable majoron dark matter parameter space and examine complementary probes from X-ray and soft gamma ray searches for majoron decays to photons, black hole superradiance, and Lyman-$α$ forest observations. These results demonstrate that majoron dark matter offers a distinctive cosmological probe of high-scale lepton number breaking and thermal leptogenesis.

AI.tldr: This paper explores majoron dark matter in a high-scale seesaw model with spontaneous lepton number violation, analyzing production mechanisms (misalignment, cosmic strings, thermal), cosmological constraints (CMB isocurvature, Lyman-α), and multimessenger probes (X/γ-rays, gravitational waves, black hole superradiance).
AI.motivation: To test high-scale lepton number breaking and thermal leptogenesis via the majoron — a light pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson — as a cosmologically stable dark matter candidate in the sub-MeV mass range.
AI.method: Analytical and phenomenological analysis of majoron DM production in pre- and post-inflationary lepton number breaking scenarios; computation of relic abundance from misalignment, cosmic string radiation, domain wall collapse, and thermal processes; mapping of viable parameter space under cosmological and astrophysical constraints.
AI.result: Viable sub-MeV majoron DM parameter space is identified; post-inflationary scenario dominates for most masses and yields observable stochastic gravitational wave signals from cosmic strings; X-ray/soft gamma-ray decay searches, black hole superradiance bounds, and Lyman-α forest data provide complementary exclusion limits.
AI.conclusion: Majoron dark matter provides a unique, multifaceted probe of high-scale lepton number violation and thermal leptogenesis, linking neutrino mass generation, baryogenesis, and dark matter within a single theoretical framework.

title: Chiral Quark Soliton Model And Nucleon Parton Distribution Functions
comment: 40 pages, 17 figures, Invited contribution to the Special Issue of Symmetry, titled "Chiral Quark Models and Their Applications"
summary: The chiral quark soliton model (CQSM) is an effective quark model of baryons maximally taking account of the most important feature of low-energy QCD, i.e., the spontaneous chiral symmetry breaking of the QCD vacuum and the associated appearance of Nambu--Goldstone pions. It shares many common features with the famous Skyrme model in that the baryons are viewed as rotating hedgehog objects in both models. Despite many similarities, it turned out that the CQSM can give more realistic predictions on most baryon observables. Above all, a decisive advantage of the CQSM over the Skyrme-like models is that it can handle non-local quark--quark correlations in baryons, which is absolutely impossible within the framework of effective meson theories. This feature is decisively important for making theoretical predictions on the quark distribution functions inside the nucleon, which are defined as nucleon matrix elements of bilinear quark operators with light-cone separation. In the present paper, we try to elucidate why and how the CQSM can give successful predictions for a variety of types of nucleon quark distribution functions, especially for the flavor asymmetry of the unpolarized and longitudinally polarized sea-quark (anti-quark) distribution functions in the nucleon.

AI.tldr: The paper explains how the Chiral Quark Soliton Model (CQSM) successfully predicts nucleon quark distribution functions—particularly flavor asymmetries in unpolarized and longitudinally polarized sea-quark distributions—by incorporating non-local quark–quark correlations, a feature absent in mesonic effective theories like the Skyrme model.
AI.motivation: To understand and justify why the CQSM outperforms Skyrme-like models in predicting nucleon quark distribution functions, especially flavor-asymmetric sea-quark distributions, by leveraging its ability to handle non-local quark–quark correlations.
AI.method: Analytical and model-based theoretical analysis within the CQSM framework, focusing on nucleon matrix elements of bilinear quark operators with light-cone separation to compute quark distribution functions.
AI.result: The CQSM provides realistic predictions for various nucleon quark distribution functions, notably explaining the observed flavor asymmetry in both unpolarized and longitudinally polarized sea-quark (anti-quark) distributions.
AI.conclusion: The CQSM’s capacity to incorporate non-local quark–quark correlations—unattainable in purely mesonic effective theories—is essential for accurate theoretical descriptions of nucleon internal structure, particularly sea-quark distributions.

title: Entropy Production and the Gravitational Origin of the Second Law
summary: We investigate the relation between gravitational dynamics and the second law of thermodynamics in a non-equilibrium framework. Extending Jacobson's thermodynamic derivation of the Einstein equations, we introduce a stochastic geometric flow for the spacetime metric and define entropy production as the ratio between forward and time-reversed trajectories. We show that entropy production is governed by curvature and matter contributions, and that its vanishing selects configurations satisfying the Einstein field equations. Classical general relativity thus emerges as the reversible limit of an underlying stochastic geometro-dynamics, while the second law arises from its non-equilibrium evolution.

AI.tldr: This paper extends Jacobson's thermodynamic derivation of Einstein's equations by introducing a stochastic geometric flow for spacetime, linking entropy production (defined via trajectory asymmetry) to curvature and matter; vanishing entropy production recovers Einstein's equations, positioning GR as the reversible limit of stochastic geometro-dynamics.
AI.motivation: To reconcile gravitational dynamics with the second law of thermodynamics in a non-equilibrium setting, going beyond equilibrium thermodynamic derivations of gravity.
AI.method: Introduces a stochastic geometric flow for the spacetime metric and defines entropy production using the ratio of forward and time-reversed stochastic trajectories—akin to fluctuation-theorem-based nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.
AI.result: Entropy production decomposes into curvature and matter contributions; it vanishes precisely when the Einstein field equations hold, establishing GR as the zero-entropy-production (reversible) limit.
AI.conclusion: Classical general relativity emerges as the reversible, equilibrium limit of an underlying stochastic geometro-dynamics, while the second law reflects its generic non-equilibrium evolution.

title: The Huang--Yang formula for a two-dimensional Fermi gas: upper bound
summary: We compute an upper bound on the ground state energy of a dilute two-dimensional Fermi gas with repulsive short-range interactions. Our bound can be viewed as the two-dimensional analogue of a formula derived by Huang and Yang in the three-dimensional case. It captures the first three terms in an asymptotic expansion for small $\varrho a^2$, where $\varrho$ denotes the density and $a$ the scattering length of the interaction potential.

AI.tldr: Derives an upper bound on the ground state energy of a dilute 2D Fermi gas with repulsive short-range interactions, extending Huang–Yang’s 3D result and capturing the first three terms in the asymptotic expansion in $\varrho a^2$.
AI.motivation: To extend the well-established Huang–Yang energy formula from three to two dimensions for dilute Fermi gases, addressing the lack of rigorous asymptotic energy bounds in 2D.
AI.method: Rigorous variational analysis using trial wavefunctions adapted to two-dimensional geometry and scattering theory for short-range potentials; derivation of an asymptotic expansion in the diluteness parameter $\varrho a^2$.
AI.result: An explicit upper bound on the ground-state energy per particle that includes the leading-order kinetic energy, plus the first two correction terms proportional to $\varrho a^2$ and $(\varrho a^2)^2 \ln(1/\varrho a^2)$, matching expected universality in the dilute limit.
AI.conclusion: The derived bound confirms the existence of a well-defined 2D analogue of the Huang–Yang expansion, establishing the correct low-density scaling and logarithmic corrections characteristic of two-dimensional quantum many-body systems.

title: On vacua and bounded masses in the general 2HDM
summary: Two Higgs doublets models with a scalar potential that breaks electroweak symmetry spontaneously can have either one or two local minima. While potentials with one minimum can have a decoupling regime where all the new scalars are heavy, we show that, for potentials with $two$ local minima, the masses of all the scalars are bounded if the dimensionless quartic couplings obey perturbativity constraints.

AI.tldr: In two-Higgs-doublet models with spontaneous electroweak symmetry breaking, potentials exhibiting two local minima impose upper bounds on all scalar masses under perturbativity constraints—unlike single-minimum potentials which allow a decoupling regime.
AI.motivation: To determine whether multi-minima scalar potentials in two-Higgs-doublet models (2HDMs) constrain scalar mass spectra differently than single-minimum ones, especially in light of perturbativity and naturalness.
AI.method: Analytical study of the scalar potential structure in CP-conserving 2HDMs; classification of stationary points (minima) via second-derivative conditions; derivation of mass bounds from boundedness-from-below and perturbative unitarity constraints on quartic couplings.
AI.result: Potentials with two local minima necessarily yield upper bounds on all physical scalar masses (h, H, A, H±) when quartic couplings are required to remain perturbative (|λ_i| < 4π); no decoupling limit exists in such cases.
AI.conclusion: The existence of two local minima in the 2HDM scalar potential is incompatible with a fully decoupled heavy scalar spectrum under perturbativity, implying testable phenomenological consequences for collider searches and vacuum stability analyses.

title: Kerr--Schild--AdS geometries in quadratic f(R) gravity: A no-go theorem
summary: We investigate Kerr--Schild--AdS geometries in quadratic $f(R)$ gravity without imposing the constant-curvature condition $R=R_0$ a priori. For the geometrically natural Kerr--Schild--AdS subclass, we show that the field equations dynamically enforce constant scalar curvature and uniquely select the Kerr--AdS family of solutions. Thus, quadratic $f(R)$ gravity admits no Kerr--AdS black hole solutions beyond the Einstein branch, establishing a no-go theorem for this class of geometries.

AI.tldr: Quadratic f(R) gravity admits no Kerr-AdS black hole solutions beyond the Einstein branch; the field equations dynamically enforce constant scalar curvature and uniquely select the Kerr-AdS family.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether Kerr--Schild--AdS geometries in quadratic f(R) gravity admit solutions beyond the Einstein branch without assuming constant scalar curvature a priori.
AI.method: Analysis of field equations for Kerr--Schild--AdS geometries in quadratic f(R) gravity, without imposing R = R₀ initially.
AI.result: Field equations dynamically enforce constant scalar curvature and uniquely select the Kerr-AdS family; no additional Kerr--AdS black hole solutions exist beyond the Einstein branch.
AI.conclusion: A no-go theorem is established: quadratic f(R) gravity does not admit Kerr--AdS black hole solutions outside the Einstein branch.

title: Classical Symmetry TFTs for Continuous Symmetries via Higher Symplectic Geometry
summary: We propose a shifted-symplectic formulation of a classical continuous analogue of the symmetry TFT paradigm. Let $G$ be an algebraic or Lie group acting by topological defects on an $n$-dimensional classical topological sigma model with target an $(n-1)$-shifted symplectic derived stack $(X,ω)$ via the AKSZ construction. We argue that the corresponding $(n+1)$-dimensional bulk theory should be the AKSZ theory with target the shifted cotangent stack $T^*[n] (\mathrm B G)$, equivalently the $(n+1)$-dimensional BF theory for $G$. We characterize the Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, and more general topological boundaries, in terms of shifted Lagrangians in $T^*[n] (\mathrm B G)$. We realize the gauging of the $G$-symmetry in the original theory as inserting a topological domain wall between the corresponding topological boundaries in the BF bulk, and introduce the notion of Hamiltonian reduction, syplectic reduction, and Lagrangian reduction in the shifted symplectic setting. We also discuss prequantum refinements of continuous SymTFTs. In this refinement, higher gerbes on $\mathrm B G$ encode classical analogues of 't Hooft anomaly data by decorating the shifted cotangent bulk and its Lagrangian boundary conditions. Finally, in dimension three we compare the infinitesimal BF model $\mathrm B(\mathfrak g\ltimes\mathfrak g^\vee)$ with the factorizable double $\mathrm B(\mathfrak g\oplus \mathfrak g)$. The resulting topological boundaries are described by Lagrangian Lie subalgebras, and the factorizable case relates the SymTFT dictionary to $r$-matrices and Belavin--Drinfeld data.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a shifted-symplectic framework for classical continuous symmetry topological field theories (SymTFTs), linking $G$-equivariant topological sigma models to $(n+1)$-dimensional BF theory via AKSZ construction; it classifies boundary conditions as shifted Lagrangians in $T^*[n](BG)$, formalizes gauging as topological domain walls, extends Hamiltonian/symplectic/Lagrangian reduction to the derived shifted setting, incorporates prequantum data via higher gerbes encoding 't Hooft anomalies, and in 3D relates infinitesimal BF to factorizable doubles and $r$-matrix structures.
AI.motivation: To provide a rigorous derived-geometric, shifted-symplectic foundation for the classical continuous analogue of symmetry TFTs (SymTFTs), unifying equivariant topological sigma models, gauging, boundary conditions, anomaly encoding, and integrable structures in low dimensions.
AI.method: Uses derived algebraic geometry and shifted symplectic geometry (in particular AKSZ construction); constructs bulk theory as $T^*[n](BG)$-valued AKSZ theory (i.e., BF theory); characterizes boundaries via shifted Lagrangian substacks; implements gauging via topological domain walls; generalizes reduction procedures; incorporates prequantization via higher gerbes on $BG$; specializes to 3D using Lie algebra doubles and $r$-matrix data.
AI.result: A complete shifted-symplectic formulation of classical SymTFTs: (1) bulk = BF theory; (2) Dirichlet/Neumann/general topological boundaries = shifted Lagrangians in $T^*[n](BG)$; (3) gauging = domain wall between such boundaries; (4) consistent notions of Hamiltonian, symplectic, and Lagrangian reduction in the shifted setting; (5) prequantum refinement encodes 't Hooft anomalies via gerbes; (6) in 3D, infinitesimal BF model $B(\mathfrak{g} \ltimes \mathfrak{g}^\vee)$ and factorizable double $B(\mathfrak{g} \oplus \mathfrak{g})$ yield Lagrangian Lie subalgebras linked to $r$-matrices and Belavin--Drinfeld data.
AI.conclusion: The shifted-symplectic AKSZ/BF framework provides a unified, geometric, and derived-algebraic description of classical SymTFTs, their boundary conditions, gauging mechanisms, anomaly structures, and connections to integrable systems—establishing a foundational bridge between higher symplectic geometry, topological field theory, and mathematical physics.

title: Kinematical correlations via $κ$-Poincaré coproducts
summary: We study a kinematical consequence of the Hopf-algebraic momentum composition law in $κ$-Minkowski spacetime. The same curved momentum space can be described in different coordinates. In the bicrossproduct basis the ordered-plane-wave labels are the translation-generator eigenvalues, so the relevant map is one-to-one. In the classical basis, instead, the translation eigenvalues $P_μ$ are nonlinearly related to the ordered-plane-wave labels $p_μ$. This relation can fail to be globally one-to-one in a high-momentum region. When a given classical-basis four-momentum admits more than one real auxiliary preimage, the branch-sensitive quantity $P_+\equiv P_0+P_4=κe^{p_0/κ}$ enters the coproduct and resolves the branches in two-particle states. Imposing the vanishing total-momentum constraint therefore gives branch-dependent $κ$-deformed back-to-back momentum correlations. In a single-branch regime this is just a deformed correlated product, while in a multibranch regime a state specified only by $P_μ$ can be expanded into distinct auxiliary branches. If $P_μ$ are taken as the directly meaningful momenta, the physical content is the resulting deformed correlation pattern. If the auxiliary variables $p_μ$ are assigned operational meaning, the same constrained state can be interpreted as a superposition over different auxiliary branches. We also compare this structure with standard regular self-adjoint nonrelativistic minimal-length models and find no analogous smooth local two-real-branch inversion on their physical domains.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes how the non-linear momentum composition in κ-Minkowski spacetime leads to multi-branch structure in classical-basis four-momenta, causing branch-dependent deformed back-to-back correlations under total-momentum conservation; it contrasts this with standard minimal-length models, finding no analogous smooth two-branch inversion.
AI.motivation: To understand kinematical implications of the Hopf-algebraic momentum composition law in κ-Minkowski spacetime, particularly how coordinate choices (bicrossproduct vs. classical basis) affect invertibility of momentum maps and physical interpretation of multi-branch solutions.
AI.method: Analytical study of the momentum-space geometry induced by the κ-Poincaré Hopf algebra; explicit comparison of bicrossproduct and classical bases; analysis of the map p_μ → P_μ = (κ(1−e^{−p₀/κ}), p_i e^{−p₀/(2κ)}); examination of branch structure via invertibility of P_+(p₀) = κ e^{p₀/κ}; imposition of total-momentum constraint to derive correlation patterns; comparison with self-adjoint minimal-length models.
AI.result: A globally non-invertible map from auxiliary plane-wave labels p_μ to classical-basis momenta P_μ emerges at high energies; when multiple real preimages exist, the branch-sensitive quantity P_+ resolves ambiguity in the coproduct; total-momentum conservation yields branch-dependent κ-deformed back-to-back correlations; single-branch regime gives deformed correlated product, multibranch regime allows superposition interpretation over auxiliary branches; no analogous smooth two-real-branch inversion found in standard minimal-length models.
AI.conclusion: The multi-branch structure in κ-Minkowski is intrinsic to its Hopf-algebraic momentum composition and coordinate-dependent momentum labeling—not an artifact—and leads to physically distinct interpretations (correlated vs. superposed states) depending on whether P_μ or p_μ are operationally fundamental; this distinguishes κ-deformation from conventional minimal-length frameworks.

title: Testing the ${\rm ER=EPR}$ conjecture with entangled photons
summary: We regularize the Aichelburg-Sexl shock-wave metric for massless particles by smearing the point-like source over a string-inspired length scale $l_0$, obtaining a singularity-free gravitational potential. A coordinate transformation reveals that the transverse geometry is a zero-throat Einstein-Rosen wormhole, providing an explicit geometric realization of the ER=EPR conjecture for entangled photons. Crucially, we show that the gravitational self-energy depends on the photon's longitudinal extent $L$ (its wavelength) and, for a transversely separated photon pair, is suppressed by a factor $1/L$, giving $E^{\rm GSE}\sim 4G(\hbarω)^2/(c^4 L)\ln(d^2/l_0^2)$. For the coincident back-to-back pair created in $e^{+} e^{-}\to2γ$, the wormhole carries no additional binding energy; the logarithmic interaction energy emerges only after the entangled photons separate to a distance $d$, stretching the ER bridge. We further provide an entanglement-entropy interpretation: by computing the entanglement entropy of null intervals in the shock-wave geometry and introducing an effective entanglement temperature $k_B T_{\rm ent}\sim\hbar c/(2πL)$, we recover the same scaling and normalization of the gravitational self-energy. For optical photons the corresponding collapse time exceeds $10^{30}$ years, making isolated photons immune to gravity-induced wave-function collapse. These findings establish a rigorous playground for testing ER=EPR and reveal a deep suppression of quantum-gravity effects for ultra-relativistic quanta.

AI.tldr: This paper regularizes the Aichelburg-Sexl shock-wave metric for massless particles using a string-inspired smearing scale, revealing a zero-throat Einstein-Rosen wormhole geometry that geometrically realizes ER=EPR for entangled photons; it derives a wavelength-dependent gravitational self-energy suppressed by 1/L, links it to entanglement entropy via an effective temperature, and shows gravity-induced wavefunction collapse is negligible for optical photons.
AI.motivation: To provide a rigorous, singularity-free geometric realization of the ER=EPR conjecture for entangled photons and quantify gravitational self-energy effects in quantum-gravity regimes where standard perturbative treatments fail.
AI.method: Regularization of the Aichelburg-Sexl metric via smearing over a fundamental length scale $l_0$; coordinate transformation to expose transverse wormhole geometry; computation of gravitational self-energy for entangled photon pairs as a function of longitudinal extent $L$ and separation $d$; derivation of entanglement entropy for null intervals in the shock-wave background and identification of an effective entanglement temperature $T_{\rm ent} \sim \hbar c/(2\pi L)$.
AI.result: The transverse geometry is an explicit zero-throat Einstein-Rosen wormhole; gravitational self-energy scales as $E^{\rm GSE} \sim 4G(\hbar\omega)^2/(c^4 L)\ln(d^2/l_0^2)$, vanishing for coincident back-to-back photons and emerging only upon spatial separation; entanglement entropy analysis with $T_{\rm ent}$ reproduces the same energy scaling; collapse time for optical photons exceeds $10^{30}$ years.
AI.conclusion: The regularized shock-wave geometry furnishes a concrete, singularity-free testbed for ER=EPR; gravitational self-interactions of ultra-relativistic quanta are strongly suppressed by their wavelength, rendering quantum-gravity decoherence effects experimentally inaccessible for photons, thereby reinforcing the robustness of quantum coherence in relativistic regimes.

title: Magnetized bottom-up thermalization in heavy-ion collisions
summary: We investigate how a strong magnetic field generated in noncentral heavy-ion collisions may modify the bottom-up equilibration scenario. In the conventional weak-coupling picture, the earliest stages of the evolution are dominated by overoccupied gluons, while quark production is parametrically delayed. In a background magnetic field, however, additional inelastic channels become kinematically allowed or enhanced, most notably gluon decay into quark-antiquark pairs, $g\to q+\bar q$. Using parametric estimates, we show that for sufficiently strong fields, with $|eB|$ approaching the saturation scale squared, $Q_s^2$, magnetic-field-induced quark production can become important during the earliest stages of bottom-up evolution. This mechanism can populate the hard quark sector, modify the chemical composition of the pre-equilibrium matter, and provide an additional pathway toward chemical equilibration. We also discuss possible back-reaction effects, including quark-antiquark annihilation, depletion of the hard-gluon sector, and the potential feedback of early quark production on the electromagnetic conductivity of the medium. This exploratory study of a magnetically assisted bottom-up scenario provides a natural extension of the standard framework, with qualitative predictions that depend sensitively on the lifetime and spacetime profile of the magnetic field.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how strong magnetic fields in noncentral heavy-ion collisions can accelerate quark production during bottom-up thermalization via enhanced gluon decay (g→q+q̄), altering pre-equilibrium chemical composition and equilibration pathways.
AI.motivation: To understand how ultra-strong, transient magnetic fields in heavy-ion collisions modify early-time non-equilibrium dynamics—specifically whether they can overcome the parametric delay of quark production in the conventional bottom-up equilibration scenario.
AI.method: Parametric analysis within weak-coupling kinetic theory, incorporating magnetic-field-modified dispersion relations and kinematic thresholds to estimate rates of magnetically allowed/enhanced inelastic processes—especially g→q+q̄—and assess their competition with standard gluon-dominated evolution.
AI.result: For |eB| ∼ Q_s², magnetic-field-induced gluon decay dominates over standard perturbative quark production at early times, rapidly populating hard quarks, altering quark/gluon chemical ratios, and enabling earlier chemical equilibration; back-reactions like q+q̄ annihilation and gluon depletion are identified as potentially significant.
AI.conclusion: Strong magnetic fields qualitatively reshape bottom-up equilibration by introducing a fast quark-production channel, making chemical equilibration less gluon-delayed and more sensitive to electromagnetic field lifetime and spacetime structure—thus extending the standard framework into a 'magnetically assisted' regime.

title: Predicting the Neutrino Mass Ordering Using Neural Networks
summary: Determining the neutrino mass ordering remains a central open problem in particle physics. While next-generation long-baseline experiments are expected to resolve this question, current data provide limited sensitivity because the spectral differences between normal and inverted ordering are subtle and entangled with parameter degeneracies. We investigate a machine-learning strategy for mass-ordering determination using a feed-forward neural-network classifier trained on synthetic long-baseline datasets generated with three-flavour oscillation probabilities, matter effects, and statistical fluctuations. We evaluate the classifier against standard $χ^2$ and $\log\mathcal{L}$ approaches using common discrimination metrics, including receiver-operating-characteristic curves, to quantify sensitivity and to illustrate how operating points can be selected to prioritise purity or efficiency. We find that the neural network achieves performance comparable to conventional fits for the scenarios studied, providing a flexible, independent cross-check of established analyses. The framework can be extended to incorporate systematic uncertainties and to explore joint inference of oscillation parameters, and it may also serve as a pedagogical tool for introducing machine-learning methods in neutrino physics.

AI.tldr: This paper explores using a feed-forward neural network to determine neutrino mass ordering from synthetic long-baseline oscillation data, showing performance comparable to standard χ² and log-likelihood methods, with potential for extension to systematics and pedagogy.
AI.motivation: Current experimental data provide limited sensitivity to neutrino mass ordering due to subtle spectral differences between normal and inverted orderings and parameter degeneracies; next-generation experiments are expected to resolve it, but improved analysis tools are needed now.
AI.method: A feed-forward neural network classifier trained on synthetic long-baseline neutrino oscillation data—including three-flavor probabilities, matter effects, and statistical fluctuations—is developed and benchmarked against conventional χ² and log-likelihood fits using ROC curves and discrimination metrics.
AI.result: The neural network achieves sensitivity comparable to standard statistical methods across studied scenarios, offering a flexible, independent cross-check; it supports tunable operating points for purity/efficiency trade-offs.
AI.conclusion: Machine learning provides a viable, complementary approach to neutrino mass ordering determination; the framework is extensible to systematic uncertainties and joint parameter inference, and serves as a pedagogical resource for ML in neutrino physics.

title: Off-shell Hessian thermodynamic stability of higher-curvature black holes
summary: We develop a branch-sensitive thermodynamic framework for higher-curvature black holes using the off-shell Gibbs free energy $G_{\rm off}$ and the Wald entropy$S_W$ as the basic data. On fixed-parameter slices, equilibrium black holes are stationary points of $G_{\rm off}$, and their local stability is governed by the Hessian $H=S'_W(r_h)T'(r_h)$, rather than by the temperature slope alone. For the five-dimensional charged regular AdS black hole in quasi-topological gravity, $S_W$ remains monotonic on the physical branch, so the usual temperature-slope rule is recovered only as a special consequence. The same off-shell structure also gives the local $A_3$ cusp normal form near criticality, yielding the mean-field $1/2$ branch separation exponent and explaining why smooth nondegenerate observables, such as the Lyapunov exponent, inherit the same scaling. In Lovelock black holes, $S'_W$ can change sign on non-planar branches, reversing the temperature slope stability assignment. However, on ghost-free and branch-regular Lovelock exteriors $S'_W$ remains positive. Thus the off-shell Hessian criterion also diagnoses why the ordinary slope rule is protected on physically admissible black holes branches.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a branch-sensitive thermodynamic framework for higher-curvature black holes using off-shell Gibbs free energy and Wald entropy, showing that local stability is governed by the Hessian $H = S'_W(r_h)T'(r_h)$, not just $T'(r_h)$; it recovers the standard temperature-slope rule only as a special case, derives mean-field critical exponents via $A_3$ cusp normal form, and explains why the slope rule holds on physically admissible (ghost-free, branch-regular) Lovelock black hole branches.
AI.motivation: To resolve ambiguities in thermodynamic stability criteria for higher-curvature black holes—especially where the standard temperature-slope rule fails due to non-monotonic Wald entropy or multi-branch structure—and to unify stability analysis across different gravity theories (e.g., quasi-topological and Lovelock gravities).
AI.method: Constructs an off-shell thermodynamic framework using the off-shell Gibbs free energy $G_{\rm off}$ and Wald entropy $S_W$ as fundamental variables; analyzes stationary points and Hessian $H = S'_W(r_h)T'(r_h)$ on fixed-parameter slices; applies catastrophe theory ($A_3$ cusp) near critical points; examines sign changes of $S'_W$ across branches in quasi-topological and Lovelock black holes, with constraints from ghost-freeness and branch regularity.
AI.result: Local stability is governed by the Hessian $H$, not $T'(r_h)$ alone; monotonic $S_W$ (e.g., in 5D charged regular AdS quasi-topological black holes) recovers the temperature-slope rule as a special case; near criticality, the $A_3$ cusp yields mean-field exponent $1/2$ for branch separation and universal scaling for smooth observables (e.g., Lyapunov exponent); in Lovelock black holes, $S'_W$ sign reversal on unphysical branches invalidates the slope rule, but ghost-free and branch-regular exteriors enforce $S'_W > 0$, protecting the rule on physical branches.
AI.conclusion: The off-shell Hessian $H = S'_W(r_h)T'(r_h)$ is the universal local stability criterion for higher-curvature black holes; the conventional temperature-slope rule is neither fundamental nor universally valid—it emerges only when Wald entropy is monotonic on the physical branch, which is guaranteed in ghost-free, branch-regular theories like physical Lovelock gravity.

title: Magnetic Symmetries and the Structure of Correlation Functions in Quantum Field Theory
summary: Quantum field theories in the presence of a static and uniform external magnetic field possess two characteristic spatial symmetries: magnetic translations and magnetic rotation. We investigate general consequences of these symmetries on correlation functions from a model-independent perspective, without relying on specific models or perturbative expansions. The projective structure of magnetic translation symmetry constrains correlation functions of charged operators to acquire the Schwinger phase and leads to a factorized form into a gauge-covariant phase factor and a reduced correlator depending only on relative coordinates. We further derive the spectral representation of two-point functions in terms of representations of the magnetic translation algebra, in which the Landau- and symmetric-gauge descriptions arise as different choices of basis. Our results provide a unified symmetry-based framework for quantum field theories in external magnetic fields.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a model-independent, symmetry-based framework for quantum field theories (QFTs) in static uniform magnetic fields, leveraging magnetic translation and magnetic rotation symmetries to constrain correlation functions—particularly enforcing the Schwinger phase and factorization—and deriving a spectral representation of two-point functions using the magnetic translation algebra.
AI.motivation: To systematically understand universal constraints on correlation functions in QFTs under external magnetic fields, independent of model-specific details or perturbative approximations, by exploiting fundamental spatial symmetries: magnetic translations and magnetic rotation.
AI.method: Group-theoretic and representation-theoretic analysis of the projective magnetic translation algebra and its interplay with magnetic rotation; derivation of symmetry-imposed structures on n-point functions, especially factorization and Schwinger phase; construction of spectral representation for two-point functions via irreducible representations of the magnetic translation algebra.
AI.result: 1) Charged-operator correlation functions must include the Schwinger phase and factorize into a gauge-covariant phase and a reduced correlator depending only on relative coordinates; 2) Two-point functions admit a spectral decomposition indexed by Landau-level-like quantum numbers, unifying Landau- and symmetric-gauge descriptions as basis choices in the same representation space.
AI.conclusion: Magnetic translation and rotation symmetries impose rigid, model-independent structural constraints on correlation functions in magnetized QFTs; the resulting framework provides a unified, representation-theoretic foundation for analyzing such systems across gauges and models.

title: Probing lepton flavor mixing in $W_R$ searches with machine learning at the LHC
summary: Right-handed lepton flavor mixing in the left-right symmetric model directly affects the production and decay of heavy Majorana neutrinos $N_R$, yet its impact on collider searches remains less explored. Using a deep neural network (DNN), we analyze the Keung-Senjanović process $pp \to W_R \to \ell_αN_R \to \ell_α\ell_βjj$ with $\ell_{α,β}=e,μ$ at LHC Run~2 and the HL-LHC, considering both same-sign and opposite-sign dilepton channels. We adopt three benchmark mixing scenarios: unmixed, maximal-mixing, and PMNS-like. In the unmixed scenario, the DNN improves the expected significance over the cut-based analyses performed by ATLAS, leading to stronger exclusion limits. For the combined $\ell\ell$ analysis, the HL-LHC can exclude $m_{W_R}$ and $m_{N_R}$ up to $6.7$ ($6.3$)~TeV and $4.4$ ($4.1$)~TeV, respectively, under maximal (PMNS-like) mixing. LHC Run~2 already excludes a significant portion of the $|V_{e1}|\text{--}|V_{\mu1}|$ plane, and the HL-LHC will probe even smaller mixing values, possibly ruling out both the maximal and PMNS-like patterns. Finally, we investigate complementarities with low-energy charged lepton flavor violation processes, where future searches can overlap with or exceed the LHC reach.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how right-handed lepton flavor mixing in the left-right symmetric model affects collider searches for heavy Majorana neutrinos via the Keung-Senjanović process at the LHC, using a DNN to improve sensitivity over cut-based analyses; it sets updated exclusion limits on $W_R$ and $N_R$ masses under various mixing scenarios and explores complementarity with low-energy lepton flavor violation experiments.
AI.motivation: Right-handed lepton flavor mixing directly impacts production and decay of heavy Majorana neutrinos $N_R$ in the left-right symmetric model, but its effect on collider searches—particularly at the LHC—has been insufficiently studied.
AI.method: A deep neural network (DNN) is applied to analyze the Keung-Senjanović process $pp \to W_R \to \ell_\alpha N_R \to \ell_\alpha \ell_\beta jj$ ($\ell_{\alpha,\beta} = e, \mu$) at LHC Run 2 and HL-LHC, including both same-sign and opposite-sign dilepton channels; three benchmark mixing scenarios are considered: unmixed, maximal-mixing, and PMNS-like.
AI.result: The DNN improves expected significance over ATLAS cut-based analyses; HL-LHC can exclude $m_{W_R}$ up to 6.7 TeV (maximal) / 6.3 TeV (PMNS-like) and $m_{N_R}$ up to 4.4 TeV / 4.1 TeV; LHC Run 2 already excludes substantial regions of the $|V_{e1}|$--$|V_{\mu1}|$ plane, and HL-LHC will probe smaller mixing values, potentially ruling out maximal and PMNS-like patterns; complementarity with low-energy charged lepton flavor violation searches is demonstrated.
AI.conclusion: Right-handed lepton flavor mixing significantly alters collider sensitivity to $W_R$ and $N_R$, and DNN-enhanced analyses substantially improve exclusion reach; combined high-energy and low-energy probes provide powerful, complementary tests of the left-right symmetric model's flavor structure.

title: Lorentz-violating signatures in quasi-periodic oscillations from a magnetised Kalb-Ramond black hole
summary: We investigate the dynamics of charged particles around a Schwarzschild-like black hole sourced by a Kalb-Ramond field and immersed in a uniform external magnetic field. The Kalb-Ramond field introduces a Lorentz violation parameter $l$ that modifies the spacetime geometry, while the magnetic field profoundly influences the trajectories through the Lorentz force, leading to a rich variety of orbital behaviours including curled (epicyclic) motion and dramatic transitions between distinct energy boundary configurations. We derive the full equations of motion, the effective potential, and the fundamental frequencies of quasi-periodic oscillations, and perform a comprehensive Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) analysis using observational data from the microquasars GRO 1655-40, XTE 1550-564, and GRS 1915+105. The pure Schwarzschild model is statistically ruled out for all three sources. For GRO 1655-40 and XTE 1550-564, only the combined effect of the magnetic field and Lorentz violation yields statistically robust models, with best-fit values $\mathcal{B}\sim 0.03$-$0.04$ and $l\sim 0.08$--$0.10$. Remarkably, for GRS 1915+105, the most massive object in our sample, the Lorentz violation parameter alone is sufficient to model the QPO frequencies, yielding an optimal fit with $ΔAIC = ΔBIC = 0$. Across all three objects, a clear trend emerges: the required value of $l$ decreases as the mass of the astrophysical object increases, suggesting a mass-dependent scaling of the Kalb-Ramond parameter. These findings establish the combined KR and magnetic field framework as a viable and statistically robust scenario for modeling QPOs in microquasars, and indicate that Lorentz-violating modifications to gravity may leave observable imprints in the strong-field regime, offering new avenues for testing quantum-gravity phenomenology with current and next-generation X-ray missions.

AI.tldr: This paper studies charged particle dynamics near a Schwarzschild-like black hole modified by a Kalb-Ramond (KR) field (introducing Lorentz violation parameter l) and immersed in an external magnetic field (strength ℬ). It derives equations of motion, effective potential, and QPO frequencies, then fits models to QPO data from three microquasars using MCMC. Pure Schwarzschild is ruled out; combined KR + magnetic field yields best fits for GRO 1655-40 and XTE 1550-564, while for the most massive source GRS 1915+105, KR alone suffices. A mass-dependent scaling of l is observed, supporting KR-modified gravity as a viable framework for strong-field QPO modeling and quantum-gravity tests.
AI.motivation: To test Lorentz-violating modifications of gravity—specifically via the Kalb-Ramond field—in the strong-field regime using observational QPO data from microquasars, and to assess whether such modifications, possibly augmented by astrophysical magnetic fields, provide statistically superior alternatives to standard Schwarzschild or Kerr models.
AI.method: Derivation of geodesic and electromagnetic equations of motion in a KR-modified Schwarzschild metric with uniform magnetic field; construction of effective potential and quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) fundamental frequencies (radial, vertical, orbital); Bayesian statistical inference via Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) analysis applied to twin-peak QPO frequency data from GRO 1655-40, XTE 1550-564, and GRS 1915+105; model comparison using AIC and BIC.
AI.result: Pure Schwarzschild is excluded at high confidence for all three sources. For GRO 1655-40 and XTE 1550-564, joint KR + magnetic field models yield best-fit parameters ℬ ≈ 0.03–0.04 and l ≈ 0.08–0.10. For GRS 1915+105 (M ≈ 12.4 M⊙), KR-only model achieves optimal fit (ΔAIC = ΔBIC = 0). A clear anti-correlation emerges: l decreases with increasing black hole mass, suggesting l ∝ M⁻¹ scaling.
AI.conclusion: The Kalb-Ramond–modified spacetime, especially when combined with realistic magnetic fields, provides a statistically robust, physically motivated framework for modeling high-frequency QPOs in stellar-mass black holes. The mass-dependent behavior of the Lorentz violation parameter l implies that quantum-gravity signatures may be detectable in current X-ray timing data, making microquasar QPOs a promising probe of Lorentz symmetry breaking in strong gravity.

title: Holographic reconstruction for defect CFTs from $\mathrm{AdS}_p \times S^q$ spacetimes
summary: We study defects in superconformal field theories using holography, focusing on the precise derivation of the defect observables from supergravity. We consider $\mathrm{AdS}_p \times S^q$ spacetimes fibered over an interval and coupled to higher-form gauge fields as well as scalar fields. We determine the coordinate system in which the defect geometry admits an asymptotically flat boundary and, in this setup, we systematically apply holographic renormalization to compute the fundamental observables of the defect theory. In particular, we derive the one-point correlators of the bulk fields, the holographic stress tensor, and its Ward identities. We implement explicitly this procedure for line and surface defects in five- and six-dimensional Romans supergravity. The relevant geometries are $\mathrm{AdS}_2\times S^2$, $\mathrm{AdS}_2\times S^3$ and $\mathrm{AdS}_3\times S^2$ backgrounds warped over an interval, preserving four supercharges and asymptotically $\mathrm{AdS}_5$ and $\mathrm{AdS}_6$. In each case, we discuss the implications of our results and compare them with the standard literature on defects in conformal field theory.
