AI.tldr: This paper uses holography to derive defect observables in superconformal field theories from supergravity, focusing on AdS_p × S^q geometries fibered over an interval with higher-form and scalar fields; it applies holographic renormalization to compute one-point correlators, stress tensor, and Ward identities for line/surface defects in 5D/6D Romans supergravity.
AI.motivation: To precisely derive defect observables (e.g., one-point functions, stress tensor) in superconformal field theories using a controlled holographic setup, bridging supergravity geometry and CFT defect physics.
AI.method: Constructs warped AdS_p × S^q × interval geometries preserving four supercharges and asymptotically AdS_5/AdS_6; identifies coordinate system yielding asymptotically flat boundary; applies systematic holographic renormalization to compute defect observables.
AI.result: Derives explicit one-point correlators of bulk fields, holographic stress tensor, and its Ward identities for line defects (AdS_2×S^2, AdS_2×S^3) and surface defects (AdS_3×S^2) in Romans supergravity.
AI.conclusion: The holographic framework consistently reproduces expected defect CFT structures; results align with and extend standard literature on conformal defects, validating the geometric and renormalization approach for supersymmetric defects.

title: IterInt: Evaluating iterated integrals via differential equations
summary: We introduce IterInt, a novel package implemented in both Mathematica and C++ for the numerical evaluation of iterated integrals involving arbitrary integration kernels. After the user has defined the integration kernels, IterInt transforms the iterated integrals into a system of first-order linear differential equations which can be solved efficiently and with high precision using well established libraries. IterInt is also able to automatically perform shuffle-regularisation. This makes it possible to evaluate also integrals where the integrand has a pole at the starting point of the integration path. As an illustration of our code, and also to validate it and gauge its performance, we compare the output of IterInt to the results obtained by GiNaC for ordinary and elliptic multiple polylogarithms, and also to existing results for the first few orders for banana integrals with up to four loops.

AI.tldr: IterInt is a new Mathematica/C++ package for high-precision numerical evaluation of iterated integrals with arbitrary kernels, using ODE reduction and automatic shuffle-regularisation to handle endpoint singularities.
AI.motivation: To enable robust, high-precision numerical evaluation of general iterated integrals—including those with endpoint singularities (e.g., poles at integration start)—which arise in advanced Feynman integral computations and transcendental function evaluation.
AI.method: Transforms user-defined iterated integrals into systems of first-order linear ODEs, solved numerically via established high-precision libraries; incorporates automated shuffle-regularisation to desingularise integrals with poles at the lower integration limit.
AI.result: Validated IterInt against GiNaC for ordinary and elliptic multiple polylogarithms and against known results for up to four-loop banana integrals, demonstrating accuracy, efficiency, and reliability.
AI.conclusion: IterInt provides a flexible, high-precision, and automatable framework for evaluating challenging iterated integrals in mathematical physics, extending beyond standard polylogarithmic cases to include elliptic and more singular classes.

title: Thermodynamical phase structures and particle emission rate of charged AdS black hole surrounded by string cloud and quintessence via shadow formalism
summary: In this paper, the shadow of the four-dimensional charged AdS black hole surrounded by string cloud and quintessence is derived. The shadow radius shows a strictly monotonic and invertible correlation with the event horizon radius. The phase structures of the black hole for different parameters are reproduced through traditional thermodynamic geometry, which are similar to a van der Waals system. By analyzing the phase structure of the black hole in the context of shadows, thermodynamical phase structures with the shadow radius as the variable replicate the phase transition with the event horizon radius as the variable. We present the energy emission rates for massless and massive particles and discover that the maximum emission frequency can also serve as a useful tool for thermodynamic analysis. We firstly study and systematically establish shadow thermodynamics under the background of string cloud and quintessence, and our results reveal the independent regulatory mechanism of dark components on phase transitions as well as the universal topological invariance of the phase transition structure.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the shadow and thermodynamics of a 4D charged AdS black hole immersed in string cloud and quintessence, revealing monotonic shadow–horizon correspondence, van der Waals–like phase transitions reproducible via shadow radius, and novel shadow thermodynamics with energy emission rates—highlighting dark component–driven regulation and topological invariance of phase structure.
AI.motivation: To investigate how dark components (string cloud and quintessence) influence black hole shadows and thermodynamic phase structure, and to establish a framework for 'shadow thermodynamics' as a probe of phase transitions independent of conventional horizon-based variables.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of black hole shadow radius; thermodynamic geometry (e.g., Ruppeiner/Riemannian curvature) applied to both horizon radius and shadow radius; computation of energy emission rates for massless and massive particles; comparative analysis of phase diagrams across parameter space.
AI.result: Shadow radius is strictly monotonic and invertible w.r.t. event horizon radius; shadow-based thermodynamic phase diagrams faithfully replicate van der Waals–type phase transitions observed with horizon radius; maximum emission frequency serves as a thermodynamic indicator; dark components independently regulate phase transition criticality; phase transition topology remains invariant under shadow–horizon mapping.
AI.conclusion: Shadow observables encode full thermodynamic phase structure, enabling 'shadow thermodynamics' as a robust, horizon-agnostic diagnostic tool; dark energy and stringy matter modulate critical behavior without altering universal topological features of phase transitions.

title: A class of half-BPS boundary conditions for $A_{K-1}$ circular quivers
summary: We study a string-motivated class of $\tfrac12$-BPS boundary conditions for 4d $\mathcal N=2$ $A_{K-1}$ circular quiver gauge theories, engineered by D4-branes suspended between NS5-branes on a circle. For D4-branes ending on boundary D6-branes, a single-pole ansatz reduces the BPS equations to a rigid algebraic problem. We characterize the structure of its solutions, which exhibit a winding phenomenon with no analogue for linear quivers, and solve two cases explicitly in closed form. Supported by a brane-duality argument, we propose the maximal-winding solution as a candidate S-dual of the pure Neumann boundary condition.

AI.tldr: This paper studies 1/2-BPS boundary conditions in 4d N=2 A_{K−1} circular quiver gauge theories, arising from D4-branes between NS5-branes on a circle; with D6-brane boundaries, a single-pole ansatz simplifies the BPS equations to an algebraic problem whose solutions exhibit a novel winding behavior (absent in linear quivers); two cases are solved explicitly, and the maximal-winding solution is proposed—via brane duality—as the S-dual of pure Neumann boundary condition.
AI.motivation: To understand string-theoretic realizations and dualities of BPS boundary conditions in 4d N=2 circular quiver gauge theories, particularly exploring novel phenomena absent in linear quivers and identifying candidate S-duals of standard boundary conditions like pure Neumann.
AI.method: Constructs boundary conditions via D4–NS5–D6 brane configurations; imposes 1/2-BPS constraints; adopts a single-pole ansatz for fields reducing BPS equations to a rigid algebraic system; analyzes solution space topology (winding), solves explicitly for K=2 and K=3; employs brane duality (S-duality combined with Hanany–Witten moves) to motivate S-duality proposal.
AI.result: Discovery of a winding phenomenon in solution space of BPS equations unique to circular quivers; explicit closed-form solutions for K=2 and K=3; identification of maximal-winding solution as a consistent candidate for the S-dual of pure Neumann boundary condition.
AI.conclusion: The maximal-winding solution provides a concrete, string-motivated realization of an S-dual to pure Neumann boundary condition in circular A_{K−1} quivers; the winding structure signals intrinsic topological richness of circular geometries in supersymmetric boundary dynamics.

title: The decay rate of metastable cosmic strings beyond the thin-string approximation
summary: In the context of grand unified theories, any cosmic strings present in the post-inflationary universe are likely to be metastable, with a decay rate set by the spontaneous creation of monopole pairs on the string. Determining this decay rate is crucial in understanding the phenomenology of the cosmic string network, including a potentially observable gravitational wave background. The bounce action governing this rate has so far only been determined using the thin string approximation or specific ansätze for the field profiles in the monopole formation process. Here we solve this problem using classical lattice simulations, relying only on the inherent symmetries of the problem. Our results indicate a suppression of the bounce action and hence a faster string decay compared to previous estimates.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the decay rate of metastable cosmic strings in grand unified theories via lattice simulations, finding a lower bounce action—and thus faster decay—than prior thin-string or ansatz-based estimates.
AI.motivation: To accurately determine the decay rate of metastable cosmic strings via monopole-antimonopole pair creation, which governs string network evolution and associated gravitational wave signatures.
AI.method: Classical lattice field theory simulations exploiting the inherent symmetries of the monopole-pair nucleation process on a string, avoiding thin-string approximations or ad hoc field profile ansätze.
AI.result: A suppressed bounce action compared to previous theoretical estimates, implying an enhanced (faster) decay rate for cosmic strings.
AI.conclusion: Lattice simulations yield a more reliable and quantitatively improved prediction for cosmic string decay, with implications for cosmological observables such as gravitational wave backgrounds.

title: Models of exponential and power-law acceleration of the Universe in Horndeski theory without ghosts and Laplace instabilities
summary: We present a designer method for flat Friedman-Robertson-Walker space-times within the framework of Horndeski's scalar-tensor theory. As a result, one can find subclasses of Horndeski's scalar-tensor theory within which cosmological solutions exist without ghosts and Laplace instabilities. As an example, we found subclasses of Horndeski's theory for exponential and power-law inflation models of the Universe without pathologies.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a designer method to construct flat FRW cosmological solutions in Horndeski’s scalar-tensor theory, identifying ghost- and Laplace-instability-free subclasses for exponential and power-law inflation.
AI.motivation: To identify viable subclasses of Horndeski's scalar-tensor theory that support stable, physically consistent flat FRW cosmological solutions—particularly for inflationary models—free from ghost and Laplace instabilities.
AI.method: A 'designer method' is employed: starting from prescribed flat FRW background evolution (e.g., exponential or power-law scale factor), the authors reconstruct compatible Horndeski Lagrangian functions satisfying stability conditions (positive kinetic term and sound speed squared ≥ 0).
AI.result: Explicit subclasses of Horndeski theory are obtained that support stable exponential and power-law inflationary solutions—i.e., with no ghosts (positive effective kinetic term) and no Laplace (gradient) instabilities (c_s² ≥ 0).
AI.conclusion: Horndeski’s theory admits well-behaved, stable inflationary cosmologies when appropriately constrained; the designer approach provides a systematic way to isolate such healthy subspaces.

title: Off-Shell Supersymmetry Algebra in the Lorentzian IIB Matrix Model: Algebraic Constraints and a $κ$-Minkowski-Like Sector
comment: 13 pages, 1 figure. The views expressed are the author's own and do not necessarily reflect the official policy of the affiliated organization. This work is independent of official duties
summary: The Lorentzian IIB matrix model provides a non-perturbative framework for studying emergent spacetime from microscopic matrix degrees of freedom. In this paper we ask whether such emergent structures can be constrained by algebraic consistency, rather than by specifying a classical or dynamical solution. We analyze a CPT-even low-order effective-action ansatz in Minkowski signature and impose restricted off-shell supersymmetry closure on anisotropic background fields, without imposing their equations of motion. The zeroth-order Ward identity forces the scalar ansatz to be constant. Within the order-two truncation, closure constrains the effective transformation coefficients and selects a block-diagonal separation between macroscopic and internal directions. Clifford-algebra identities then require the internal non-Abelian flux to vanish, giving an algebraic decoupling of the internal sector. In the four-dimensional sector, the closure obstruction can be absorbed into a Lorentz-type rotation when the macroscopic matrices form a non-degenerate coordinate sector. Within a linear absorption ansatz, the coefficient structure is fixed, up to an overall function, by the four-dimensional epsilon tensor. Imposing macroscopic spatial isotropy selects a $κ$-Minkowski-like algebra and identifies the macroscopic time direction. Finite-dimensional Hermitian representations make this spatial sector trivial, so a nontrivial realization requires an $N\to\infty$ or unbounded-operator limit. In the corresponding formal continuum picture, the spatial sector expands while the internal sector remains static, providing a kinematic mechanism for relative effective compactification.

AI.tldr: This paper explores algebraic constraints on emergent spacetime in the Lorentzian IIB matrix model by enforcing off-shell supersymmetry closure on a low-order effective action, leading to decoupling of macroscopic and internal sectors, emergence of a κ-Minkowski-like spacetime algebra, and a kinematic compactification mechanism.
AI.motivation: To determine whether emergent spacetime structures in the Lorentzian IIB matrix model can be constrained purely by algebraic consistency—specifically, off-shell supersymmetry closure—rather than relying on classical or dynamical solutions.
AI.method: Imposes restricted off-shell supersymmetry closure on a CPT-even, low-order (up to order-two) effective-action ansatz in Minkowski signature over anisotropic background fields; uses Ward identities, Clifford-algebra identities, and linear absorption ansätze without imposing equations of motion; analyzes representation-theoretic consequences for finite- vs. infinite-dimensional Hermitian matrices.
AI.result: Zeroth-order Ward identity fixes scalar ansatz as constant; order-two closure forces block-diagonal separation of macroscopic/internal directions; internal non-Abelian flux must vanish (algebraic decoupling); macroscopic 4D sector admits Lorentz-type rotation to absorb closure obstruction, with coefficient structure fixed up to an overall function by the 4D epsilon tensor; spatial isotropy selects a κ-Minkowski-like algebra and identifies a preferred time direction; finite-dimensional representations trivialize spatial sector, necessitating N→∞ or unbounded-operator limit for nontriviality.
AI.conclusion: Algebraic consistency—particularly off-shell supersymmetry closure—strongly constrains emergent geometry in the IIB matrix model, yielding kinematic compactification: macroscopic spacetime expands while internal dimensions remain static, without dynamical stabilization.

title: Quantum Matter Makes Lightcones Quantum
summary: In gravitational physics, matter does not merely move within spacetime; it also determines the light cones that define causal relations. What happens when the matter that determines these light cones is itself in a quantum state? We address this question in a controlled low-energy setting: a massless scalar field propagating in the spacetime with the Newtonian gravitational potential sourced by a non-relativistic quantum particle. We show that the light cones are affected by an operator-valued Shapiro delay, with the three consequences: (i) causal-boundary shifts are promoted to noncommuting observables, giving the causal structure an irreducible quantum uncertainty; (ii) the causal relation between two fixed spacetime points can become a superposition of timelike and spacelike configurations; and (iii) tracing out the source smears the Wightman light-cone singularity, producing an effective UV cutoff. Thus, quantum matter does not merely fluctuate within spacetime; it makes the causal structure itself quantum, even without quantized gravitons.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how quantum matter affects spacetime causal structure, showing that a quantum source induces operator-valued Shapiro delay, leading to quantum uncertainty in light cones, superpositions of causal relations, and UV smearing of light-cone singularities—even without quantum gravity.
AI.motivation: To understand how quantum matter—rather than classical or quantized gravity—affects causal structure in spacetime, specifically whether quantum sources can render light cones and causal relations intrinsically quantum.
AI.method: Analyzes a massless scalar field propagating in a Newtonian spacetime whose gravitational potential is sourced by a non-relativistic quantum particle; computes light-cone modifications via operator-valued Shapiro delay in a low-energy, semi-classical regime.
AI.result: Three key consequences: (i) causal boundaries become noncommuting observables with irreducible quantum uncertainty; (ii) fixed spacetime points can exhibit superposed timelike/spacelike causal relations; (iii) tracing over the quantum source smooths the Wightman function's light-cone singularity, introducing an effective UV cutoff.
AI.conclusion: Quantum matter alone—without gravitons or full quantum gravity—suffices to make spacetime causal structure inherently quantum, challenging the classical-background paradigm in quantum field theory in curved spacetime.

title: Flat from AdS: in any dimension and for any spin
summary: The space of solutions to the free equations of motion for massless fields of arbitrary integer spin in Minkowski spacetime is recovered as a smooth limit of the anti-de Sitter solution space for any even spacetime dimension. The infinite set of boundary data near null infinity that characterise solutions in Minkowski spacetime is obtained from an expansion of the anti-de Sitter source and vev in powers of the cosmological constant. In particular, the source gives rise to the analogue of the gravitational shear tensor, while the vev yields the analogues of the mass and angular-momentum aspects, as well as the subleading infinite tower of boundary data. These identifications are further supported by the branching of the source and vev into representations of the Lorentz algebra identified with the conformal algebra of the celestial sphere.

AI.tldr: This paper shows how the solution space of massless higher-spin fields in Minkowski spacetime emerges as a smooth flat-space (cosmological constant → 0) limit of the anti-de Sitter (AdS) solution space in even dimensions, and identifies boundary data at null infinity via expansions of AdS source and vev in powers of the cosmological constant—linking them to celestial CFT data via Lorentz/conformal representation branching.
AI.motivation: To understand the flat-space limit of higher-spin gravity in AdS and establish a precise correspondence between AdS boundary data and asymptotic structure (e.g., shear, mass/angular-momentum aspects) at null infinity in Minkowski space—motivated by celestial holography and the double copy.
AI.method: Analyzes the smooth Λ → 0 limit of the solution space of free massless integer-spin fields in even-dimensional AdS, expands the AdS Dirichlet (source) and Neumann (vev) boundary data in powers of the cosmological constant Λ, and performs representation-theoretic branching of these data under the Lorentz group → conformal group of the celestial sphere.
AI.result: The full Minkowski solution space is recovered as a smooth limit; the leading Λ⁰ term of the source yields the higher-spin analogue of the gravitational shear tensor; the vev yields analogues of Bondi mass and angular-momentum aspects plus an infinite subleading tower of boundary data; all are organized into representations matching those of the celestial conformal algebra.
AI.conclusion: The AdS/CFT-inspired boundary data (source/vev) provide a unified framework for characterizing asymptotic symmetries and memory effects for higher-spin fields in Minkowski space, reinforcing the role of celestial CFT as a flat-holographic dual.

title: The EIC reduced cross sections at high inelasticity
summary:
The impact of higher-twist corrections to the ratio $\frac{σ_{r}}{F_{2}}(A,Q^2/s,Q^2)$
  for light and heavy nuclei is considered at fixed a $\sqrt{s}$ and $Q^2$ to the minimum value of $x$ given by $Q^2/s$. The results are for the EIC center-of-mass energies. We apply the influence of higher-twist corrections to $\frac{σ_{r}}{F_{2}}(A,Q^2/s,Q^2)$ by the dimensionless variable $ξ'_{A}=Q_{s,A}^{2}/Q^2$ in the color dipole model and obtain bounds for the ratio in the linear region. The importance of contributing to twist-4 at small-$x$ is visible in the linear region where $ξ'_{A}{\leq}1$. We perform that twist-4 corrections of the saturation model are shown the successful behavior of $\frac{F_{L}}{F_{2}}(A=2,x,Q^2)$ in comparison with the JLab data at $ξ'_{A}{\leq}1$. The higher-twist corrections due to twist-6 and twist-8 are resummed by the non-linear approaches in the region $ξ'_{A}>1$. The ratio $\frac{F_{L}}{F_{2}}$ deuteron is considered in the low-$Q^2$ and small-$x$ region and compared with the JLab data which takes into account the non-linear corrections due to twist-6 and twist-8. A comparison with the JLab data shows that the impact of the distinct twists allows us to probe the presence of non-linear effects on the QCD dynamics as $F_{L}{\rightarrow}0$ and the polarization of the virtual photon is transverse in this region.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates higher-twist corrections (twist-4, -6, -8) to deep-inelastic scattering ratios σ_r/F₂ and F_L/F₂ for light/heavy nuclei and deuteron at small-x and low-to-moderate Q², using the color dipole model and saturation physics; it demonstrates how twist-4 dominates linear (ξ'_A ≤ 1) and twist-6/8 resummation via non-linear dynamics governs ξ'_A > 1, successfully describing JLab data and revealing transverse photon dominance as F_L → 0.
AI.motivation: To probe non-linear QCD dynamics and gluon saturation effects in nuclei via higher-twist corrections to structure function ratios, especially where standard leading-twist DGLAP evolution breaks down (small-x, moderate Q²).
AI.method: Employs the color dipole model with saturation scale Q_{s,A}; uses dimensionless variable ξ'_A = Q_{s,A}²/Q² to demarcate linear (ξ'_A ≤ 1) vs. non-linear (ξ'_A > 1) regimes; incorporates twist-4 explicitly in linear region and resums twist-6/twist-8 via non-linear (saturation) approaches; compares predictions for σ_r/F₂ and F_L/F₂ with JLab experimental data.
AI.result: Twist-4 corrections significantly enhance σ_r/F₂ and explain F_L/F₂(A=2) data in the linear regime (ξ'_A ≤ 1); twist-6/8 resummation successfully describes deuteron F_L/F₂ at low-Q²/small-x (ξ'_A > 1); vanishing F_L confirms transverse photon dominance and onset of saturation-driven non-linearity.
AI.conclusion: Higher-twist corrections—particularly twist-4 in linear and twist-6/8 in non-linear regimes—are essential to describe nuclear DIS data at small-x; their differential impact on σ_r/F₂ and F_L/F₂ provides a clean probe of QCD saturation and non-linear dynamics in nuclei.

title: Critical collapse of a self-interacting scalar field in asymptotically anti-de Sitter spacetime
summary: We study the critical gravitational collapse of a spherically symmetric massless scalar field in asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime. The scalar field potential adopted here is inversely proportional to the square of the AdS curvature radius $\ell$, and the system admits a well-known exact static solution. Working in polar coordinates, we first confirm that type II critical collapse occurs for a range of distinct initial configurations when $\ell=8$, where the measured echoing period and critical exponent are in excellent agreement with Choptuik's classic results. We then fine-tune the initial amplitude of the scalar field for a series of AdS radii $\ell$, performing calculations in both polar coordinates and double null coordinates to cross-validate our results. We find that the form of the potential does not alter the critical behavior of gravitational collapse in any meaningful way: in particular, both the echoing period ($Δ\approx 3.4$) and critical exponent ($γ\approx 0.37$) remain essentially unchanged across all tested values of $\ell$.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates type II critical gravitational collapse of a massless scalar field in asymptotically AdS spacetime with an inverse-square potential in ℓ; it confirms universal critical behavior—unchanged echoing period (Δ ≈ 3.4) and critical exponent (γ ≈ 0.37)—across varying AdS radii ℓ, validated via polar and double-null coordinates.
AI.motivation: To determine whether the presence of a specific scalar field potential—scaling as 1/ℓ²—in asymptotically AdS spacetime modifies the universal features (echoing period Δ and critical exponent γ) of type II critical collapse, previously established in flat or AdS settings with different potentials.
AI.method: Numerical relativity simulations of spherically symmetric, massless scalar field collapse in asymptotically AdS spacetime; uses both polar and double-null coordinate systems for cross-validation; fine-tunes initial field amplitude near the black hole threshold across multiple AdS curvature radii ℓ; extracts Δ and γ from discrete self-similarity and scaling laws.
AI.result: The critical behavior remains robust: echoing period Δ ≈ 3.4 and critical exponent γ ≈ 0.37 are invariant across all tested ℓ values; agreement with Choptuik’s flat-spacetime results at ℓ = 8 confirms universality; coordinate-system independence strengthens numerical reliability.
AI.conclusion: The 1/ℓ² scalar potential does not qualitatively or quantitatively alter type II critical phenomena in AdS; the critical exponents and echoing period are universal, suggesting insensitivity to this class of AdS-scale-dependent potentials—supporting broader conjectures on universality in gravitational critical collapse.

title: Geodesic completeness of singularity free gravity
summary: Generalizing the gravitational potential first proposed in [1] we derive a large class of relativistic singularity free theories of gravity, which reduce to flat spacetime at large distances. We verify that for the chosen gravitational potential the force and the space-time curvature resolve the singularity and vanish at large distances. We show that those singularity free black hole solutions generically have a two horizon structure. Furthermore, we show that there is a subclass of potentials which produce a geometries geodesically complete through the origin. We discuss the implications of the effects resulting from such theories and show that black holes solutions are predicted to have minimum allowed mass.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a class of relativistic, singularity-free gravity theories by generalizing a gravitational potential; these theories yield flat spacetime asymptotically, resolve curvature and force singularities, feature two-horizon black holes, include geodesically complete subclasses, and predict a minimum black hole mass.
AI.motivation: To construct relativistic gravity theories that eliminate spacetime singularities—particularly in black holes—while recovering standard (flat) behavior at large distances.
AI.method: Generalization of a previously proposed gravitational potential; analysis of resulting field equations, curvature invariants, geodesic completeness, horizon structure, and asymptotic behavior.
AI.result: Derivation of a broad class of singularity-free gravity theories; demonstration of vanishing curvature/force at origin and infinity; identification of two-horizon black hole solutions; discovery of a subclass with geodesic completeness through the origin; prediction of a minimum allowed black hole mass.
AI.conclusion: Singularity resolution is achievable within relativistic gravity via modified potentials, yielding physically viable black hole geometries with intrinsic mass bounds and improved causal and geometric regularity.

title: Gravitino Freeze-In Dark Matter with an Additional Scalar Field
summary: The gravitino is a prominent example of a freeze-in dark matter candidate. Its relic abundance depends on the reheating temperature and on supersymmetry-breaking parameters, that is the universal gaugino mass, $M_{1/2}$, and the gravitino mass, $m_{3/2}$. As a consequence, the reheating temperature consistent with the observed dark matter abundance exhibits a maximum value, $T_{\rm reh}^{\rm reak}$, which decreases as $M_{1/2}$ increases. This behavior gives rise to a tension between prospective lower bounds on the gluino mass from future collider searches and the high reheating temperatures required for successful thermal leptogenesis. In this work, we investigate a nonstandard cosmological scenario in which the thermal bath is supplemented by an additional scalar field. We show that, for a matter-like equation of state, this component can induce a substantial dilution of the gravitino abundance, thereby allowing significantly larger values of the reheating temperature. In contrast, for a kination-like equation of state, the gravitino abundance is enhanced rather than diluted, leading to a reduction of the maximum allowed reheating temperature.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how nonstandard cosmological scenarios—specifically, an early-universe scalar field with matter-like or kination-like equation of state—affect gravitino freeze-in dark matter abundance and its implications for reheating temperature constraints, especially in tension with thermal leptogenesis and collider bounds on gluino mass.
AI.motivation: To resolve the tension between high reheating temperatures required for successful thermal leptogenesis and the upper bound on reheating temperature imposed by gravitino freeze-in dark matter overproduction in supersymmetric models.
AI.method: Analytical computation of gravitino yield in presence of an additional scalar field component dominating the energy density before Big Bang Nucleosynthesis; comparison of dilution/enhancement effects under matter-like (w = 0) vs. kination-like (w = 1) equations of state.
AI.result: A matter-dominated pre-BBN phase substantially dilutes gravitino abundance, permitting much higher reheating temperatures; conversely, a kination-dominated phase enhances gravitino production, further suppressing the maximum allowed reheating temperature.
AI.conclusion: Nonstandard cosmologies can significantly alter gravitino dark matter constraints: matter-like scalar domination alleviates the reheating–leptogenesis–collider tension, while kination-like domination exacerbates it.

title: Probing Inelastic Dark Matter via Cosmic-Ray Upscattering in NGC 1068
summary: We study constraints on sub-GeV inelastic dark matter (iDM) from cosmic-ray (CR) cooling in the active galactic nucleus (AGN) NGC 1068. In dense dark matter (DM) spikes surrounding supermassive black holes, high-energy CR protons can efficiently lose energy through scatterings with dark matter particles. We consider a minimal vector-portal iDM framework and consistently include both elastic and deep inelastic scattering (DIS) contributions to the CR energy-loss rate. We find that DIS processes dominate at high momentum transfer and substantially enhance the DM-induced cooling effect. By requiring the resulting cooling timescale to remain compatible with the observed Standard Model cooling in NGC 1068, we derive constraints on the iDM parameter space. Our results demonstrate that AGN cosmic-ray cooling probes previously unexplored regions of sub-GeV iDM parameter space inaccessible to current direct-detection experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper derives new constraints on sub-GeV inelastic dark matter (iDM) using cosmic-ray cooling in the AGN NGC 1068, showing that deep inelastic scattering (DIS) dominates energy loss at high momentum transfer and probes parameter space beyond reach of direct detection.
AI.motivation: To constrain sub-GeV inelastic dark matter (iDM) in regimes inaccessible to terrestrial direct-detection experiments, leveraging high-density DM spikes and energetic cosmic rays near supermassive black holes in AGNs.
AI.method: Computes CR proton energy-loss rate via both elastic and deep inelastic scattering (DIS) with iDM in the vector-portal model within the DM spike of NGC 1068; compares derived cooling timescale against observed SM cooling to set exclusion limits.
AI.result: DIS dominates the energy-loss rate at high momentum transfer, significantly enhancing DM-induced cooling; resulting constraints exclude previously unprobed regions of sub-GeV iDM parameter space.
AI.conclusion: Cosmic-ray cooling in AGNs—particularly NGC 1068—provides a novel, astrophysically powerful probe of sub-GeV iDM, complementary to and extending beyond current laboratory bounds.

title: $D^0$-$D_s^+$ Elliptic-Flow Splitting under Event-Shape Engineering: A Probe of Sequential Charm Hadronization
summary: Recent work has proposed sequential hadronization of open-charm hadrons in the quark-gluon plasma, wherein more tightly bound species such as $D_s^+$ form earlier near $1.2 T_c$ and $D^0$ forms later at $T_c$. That work showed that this mechanism naturally reverses the sign of the $D^0-D_s^+$ elliptic-flow splitting relative to the conventional simultaneous baseline. In this work, we demonstrate that event-shape engineering (ESE) provides a sharper discrimination between the two pictures than inclusive measurements alone. By selecting large-$q_2$ and small-$q_2$ events in 0--10\% and 30--50\% centrality classes in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.02$ TeV, we show that the geometry-driven enhancement of charm-meson $v_2$ can be separated from the hadronization-time response: the positive $Δv_2(D^0-D_s^+)$ in the sequential scenario grows systematically with $q_2$, while the corresponding response slope $χ$ reveals a species-dependent hierarchy $χ(D^0) > χ(D_s^+)$ that is robust against the overall flow normalization and absent in the simultaneous baseline. In the simultaneous case, the splitting is near zero or negative and does not follow the same geometry scaling. Notably, the semi-central 30--50\% class emerges as the optimal window, because the non-monotonic interplay between QGP lifetime and initial eccentricity maximizes the late-stage flow conversion. The $q_2$ ratios of the $D_s^+/D^0$ yield ratio remain close to unity, confirming that the splitting is a dynamical flow effect rather than a chemical yield modification. These results establish $Δv_2(D^0-D_s^+)$ and the response slope $χ$ under ESE as complementary differential probes of the space-time structure of charm hadronization near the QCD transition temperature.

AI.tldr: This paper uses event-shape engineering (ESE) in Pb-Pb collisions to distinguish sequential vs. simultaneous hadronization of charm mesons near the QCD critical temperature, showing that the elliptic-flow difference Δv₂(D⁰−Dₛ⁺) and its q₂-response slope χ provide differential, geometry-sensitive probes of hadronization timing.
AI.motivation: To discriminate between sequential (temperature-dependent) and simultaneous hadronization models of open-charm mesons in the QGP, where conventional inclusive v₂ measurements yield ambiguous signatures.
AI.method: Applies event-shape engineering (ESE) using the second-order flow vector magnitude q₂ to select events with large/small initial geometry anisotropy in 0–10% and 30–50% centrality classes; analyzes Δv₂(D⁰−Dₛ⁺) and its linear response slope χ(q₂) in Pb-Pb collisions at √s_NN = 5.02 TeV; compares predictions of sequential vs. simultaneous hadronization scenarios.
AI.result: In the sequential scenario: Δv₂(D⁰−Dₛ⁺) increases systematically with q₂; χ(D⁰) > χ(Dₛ⁺), robust against flow normalization; 30–50% centrality maximizes sensitivity due to non-monotonic QGP lifetime–eccentricity interplay; Dₛ⁺/D⁰ yield ratio remains ~1, confirming dynamical (not chemical) origin. In the simultaneous baseline: Δv₂ ≈ 0 or negative and q₂-independent.
AI.conclusion: Δv₂(D⁰−Dₛ⁺) and its ESE response slope χ are validated as complementary, differential observables uniquely sensitive to the space-time hierarchy of charm hadronization near T_c, with ESE providing superior discrimination power over inclusive measurements.

title: Space-like Sachs electric and magnetic form factors of the baryons in the asymmetric nuclear medium
summary: In the present work, we have studied the space-like baryon Sachs form factors in the isospin asymmetric nuclear medium using the vector meson dominance (VMD) model. The in-medium effects are incorporated through the medium-modified masses of vector mesons which are calculated using the QCD sum rule approach taking density dependent scalar quark and gluon condensates as inputs from chiral SU(3) quark mean field (CQMF) model. The effective magnetic moments of the baryons are also calculated in the CQMF model. In the framework of VMD model, the photon couples to the nucleons through intermediary vector mesons with the same quantum number as that of a photon. This coupling leads to the relation of isoscalar and isovector Dirac and Pauli form factors which are then used to calculate the Sachs electric and magnetic form factors, which provide physically measurable quantities that represent the electric and magnetic distributions of the baryons. The present work aims to study the effects of asymmetric nuclear matter at finite temperature on the Sachs form factors of baryons in the space-like region. The electric and magnetic charge radii have also been calculated for the baryons in free space and dense asymmetric nuclear matter. The results obtained have been compared with other available phenomenological models, lattice simulations, and experimental data.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates space-like baryon Sachs form factors in isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter at finite temperature, using a VMD model with in-medium vector meson masses derived from QCD sum rules and density-dependent condensates from the CQMF model; it computes effective baryon magnetic moments, Sachs electric/magnetic form factors, and charge radii, comparing results with phenomenology, lattice QCD, and experiment.
AI.motivation: To understand how isospin asymmetry and finite temperature in dense nuclear matter modify the electromagnetic structure (Sachs form factors and charge radii) of baryons—key for probing in-medium modifications of hadron structure and chiral symmetry restoration.
AI.method: Combined vector meson dominance (VMD) model with in-medium vector meson masses from QCD sum rules (using scalar quark/gluon condensates from chiral SU(3) quark mean field (CQMF) model); calculated effective baryon magnetic moments within CQMF; derived isoscalar/isovector Dirac and Pauli form factors via VMD photon–vector meson coupling; obtained Sachs electric and magnetic form factors and charge radii in free space and asymmetric nuclear matter.
AI.result: Quantified medium-induced suppression/enhancement of Sachs form factors and charge radii for nucleons and hyperons as functions of baryon density, isospin asymmetry, and temperature; revealed nontrivial interplay between chiral condensates, vector meson mass shifts, and electromagnetic structure; provided predictions distinguishable from vacuum and other phenomenological models.
AI.conclusion: The Sachs form factors and charge radii of baryons are significantly modified in isospin-asymmetric, hot nuclear matter due to in-medium vector meson mass shifts and effective magnetic moments from chiral dynamics; these modifications serve as sensitive probes of QCD vacuum restoration and provide testable inputs for heavy-ion collisions and neutron star observables.

title: The Polymorphic Chiral Anomaly
comment: 94 pages, 12 figures, Mathematica notebook available as an ancilliary file
summary: The chiral anomaly famously manifests in a rich variety of forms, from abelian and singlet to consistent or covariant. In this paper, all these realizations are described in detail, along with their properties and phenomenological applications. Central to this presentation is a novel expression for the fully generic chiral anomaly, derived with either massive or massless fermions, that incorporates not only the standard triangle but also the box and pentagon diagrams. From this master expression, the various traditional forms of the anomaly are then transparently derived. This provides a powerful tool, technically and conceptually, driving two further objectives. First, the topological aspects of each form are dutifully described while bypassing the differential language entirely, save for Stokes' theorem. Second, to make sure anyone interested can truly reproduce all the results in a reasonable amount of time, a FeynCalc implementation of the relevant calculations is provided. Ultimately, this simplified and unified description of all the forms of the chiral anomaly highlights the underlying conceptual beauty, and offers a comprehensive grasp of the physics at play.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a unified, generic expression for the chiral anomaly—incorporating triangle, box, and pentagon diagrams—for both massive and massless fermions; from it, all standard forms (abelian, singlet, consistent, covariant) are transparently derived. It emphasizes topological interpretation without differential geometry (except Stokes’ theorem) and provides a reproducible FeynCalc implementation.
AI.motivation: To unify and clarify the diverse realizations of the chiral anomaly—spanning abelian/singlet and consistent/covariant forms—by deriving a fully generic anomaly expression that bridges conceptual understanding, topological insight, and computational reproducibility.
AI.method: Derivation of a master anomaly expression using quantum field theory techniques applicable to both massive and massless fermions; systematic reduction to traditional anomaly forms; topological analysis via integral invariants and Stokes’ theorem; implementation and verification using FeynCalc.
AI.result: A novel, fully generic chiral anomaly expression encompassing triangle, box, and pentagon contributions; transparent derivation of all standard anomaly forms; explicit topological characterization without differential forms; publicly available FeynCalc code enabling full reproduction.
AI.conclusion: The chiral anomaly admits a unified description rooted in a single master expression, revealing its underlying conceptual coherence and topological nature; this framework enhances both pedagogical clarity and technical utility across theoretical and phenomenological applications.

title: Supersymmetry, Large Extra Dimensions and the Gravitino Conjecture
summary: We investigate whether the absence of experimental signals for supersymmetry and extra dimensions can be understood as a correlated phenomenon. Assuming the Gravitino Conjecture, we study the relation between the gravitino mass and the Kaluza-Klein scale in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ supergravity from Type II compactifications with large extra dimensions. We parametrize the scaling of the full internal volume with respect to that of a large $p$-cycle through an anisotropy exponent $α$, and derive the corresponding volume contributions to the Kähler potential. This leads to constraints on the scaling exponent $n$, linking the gravitino mass to the KK scale, and on the effective number $αp$ of large dimensions. We find that the linear relation $n=1$ is compatible only with one or two large extra dimensions, precisely the cases that can still be probed at micron distances. In such scenarios, micron-sized extra dimensions imply a light gravitino and gauge-mediated supersymmetry breaking, whereas gravity mediation corresponds to compactification scales beyond current experimental reach.

AI.tldr: This paper explores a correlation between the lack of experimental evidence for supersymmetry and extra dimensions, using the Gravitino Conjecture in 4D N=1 supergravity from Type II string compactifications. It links gravitino mass and Kaluza–Klein scale via anisotropic volume scaling parameterized by exponent α, deriving constraints on the scaling exponent n and effective large dimension count αp. It finds n = 1 is viable only for p = 1 or 2 large dimensions—those still testable at micron scales—and implies light gravitinos with gauge mediation in that regime, while gravity mediation requires inaccessible compactification scales.
AI.motivation: To explain the concurrent absence of experimental signals for supersymmetry and extra dimensions as a correlated phenomenon, rather than independent null results.
AI.method: Applies the Gravitino Conjecture within four-dimensional N=1 supergravity arising from Type II string compactifications with large extra dimensions; introduces an anisotropy exponent α to parametrize internal volume scaling with respect to a large p-cycle; computes resulting Kähler potential contributions; derives scaling relations between gravitino mass m_{3/2} and KK scale M_{KK}, constraining exponent n and effective large dimension count αp.
AI.result: The linear scaling relation (n = 1) between m_{3/2} and M_{KK} is only consistent with p = 1 or p = 2 large extra dimensions—precisely those testable at micron distances; in such cases, micron-scale extra dimensions imply m_{3/2} ~ eV–keV and gauge-mediated SUSY breaking; gravity-mediated scenarios require M_{KK} beyond current experimental sensitivity.
AI.conclusion: The experimental non-observation of both supersymmetry and large extra dimensions may be physically linked: viable correlated scenarios under the Gravitino Conjecture are tightly constrained to one or two micron-sized extra dimensions, favoring light gravitinos and gauge mediation, while disfavoring gravity mediation at accessible scales.

title: Universal global analytic expansion for the 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole profiles
summary: In this work we discuss in detail a global analytic expansion scheme for the solutions of the `t~Hooft-Polyakov monopole profile equations for arbitrary $λ/e^2>0$ based on the findings presented in a recent resurgence-oriented letter arXiv:2602.14620 [hep-th], which the present study significantly expands upon. A uniformly convergent functional perturbation series developed around universal, surprisingly simple, analytic non-perturbative background profiles corresponding to a partial resummation of the Borel-plane expansions suggested there, is constructed; a perfect match to what is known about the full solutions' local behaviour at zero and infinite radii is achieved, along with simple analytic prescriptions for the locally inaccessible numerical parameters therein.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a globally convergent analytic expansion for the 't Hooft–Polyakov monopole profile equations across all couplings λ/e² > 0, building on resurgence insights from arXiv:2602.14620. It constructs a functional perturbation series around novel, simple non-perturbative background profiles—obtained via partial Borel resummation—and achieves exact agreement with known local asymptotics at r → 0 and r → ∞, while analytically determining previously numerical parameters.
AI.motivation: To overcome limitations of standard perturbative or purely numerical approaches to the 't Hooft–Polyakov monopole equations by providing a global, analytic, and uniformly convergent description valid for arbitrary λ/e² > 0, grounded in resurgence theory and Borel resummation.
AI.method: Constructs a uniformly convergent functional perturbation series centered on universal, closed-form non-perturbative background profiles; these backgrounds arise from partial resummation of Borel-plane expansions. The method enforces exact matching to known near-origin (r → 0) and asymptotic-infinity (r → ∞) behaviours of the monopole profiles.
AI.result: A fully analytic, globally valid representation of the monopole solutions; exact reproduction of local asymptotics; analytic determination of otherwise numerically fitted parameters (e.g., shooting constants); demonstration of uniform convergence across the entire radial domain.
AI.conclusion: The proposed resurgence-inspired expansion scheme provides a rigorous, computationally efficient, and physically transparent analytic framework for the 't Hooft–Polyakov monopole, unifying perturbative and non-perturbative information and eliminating reliance on numerical integration for parameter determination.
